translations.idiomatic: Treatise 82

sentences.zh: 選舉二

translations.literal: Selection and Examinations 2.
translations.idiomatic: Selection and Examinations, Part 2

sentences.zh: 學校二

translations.literal: Schools 2.
translations.idiomatic: Schools, Part 2

sentences.zh: 學校新制之沿革，略分二期。

translations.literal: The evolution of the new school system may be broadly divided into two periods.
translations.idiomatic: The development of the modern school system falls roughly into two periods.

sentences.zh: 同治初迄光緒辛丑以前，為無系統教育時期；

translations.literal: From the early Tongzhi reign until before the Xinchou year of the Guangxu reign was the period of unsystematic education;
translations.idiomatic: From the early Tongzhi era down to the year before the 1901 reforms (Xinchou) was the period of education without a unified system;

sentences.zh: 辛丑以後迄宣統末，為有系統教育時期。

translations.literal: From after Xinchou until the end of the Xuantong reign was the period of systematic education.
translations.idiomatic: from the Xinchou reforms through the end of the Xuantong reign was the period of systematic education.

sentences.zh: 自五口通商，英法聯軍入京後，朝廷鑒於外交挫衄，非興學不足以圖強。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the five treaty ports and the entry of the Anglo-French allied forces into the capital, the court, seeing setbacks in foreign relations, recognized that without promoting learning there would be insufficient means to seek strength.
translations.idiomatic: After the opening of the treaty ports and the Anglo-French occupation of Beijing, the court saw how diplomacy had failed and concluded that national strength could not be achieved without promoting education.

sentences.zh: 先是交涉重任，率假手無識牟利之通事，往往以小嫌釀大釁，至是始悟通事之不可恃。

translations.literal: Previously the heavy burden of negotiation was generally entrusted to ignorant interpreters who sought profit; small grievances often brewed into great disputes, and only then did they realize that interpreters could not be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, weighty diplomatic business had usually been left to ignorant, profit-seeking interpreters, who often turned minor friction into major incidents; only now did the government grasp that such men could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 又震於列強之船堅砲利，急須養成繙譯與製造船械及海陸軍之人才。

translations.literal: They were also shaken by the powerful nations' stout ships and sharp cannon, and urgently needed to cultivate talent in translation, ship and ordnance manufacture, and naval and land forces.
translations.idiomatic: Shocked as well by the Western powers' modern fleets and artillery, the state urgently needed to train men in translation, shipbuilding and armaments, and naval and military service.

sentences.zh: 故其時首先設置之學校，曰京師同文館，曰上海廣方言館，曰福建船政學堂及南北洋水師、武備等學堂。

translations.literal: Therefore the schools first established at that time were: the Tongwen Guan in the capital, the Guangfangyan Guan in Shanghai, the Fujian Naval Administration School, and the naval and military academies of the Northern and Southern Fleets.
translations.idiomatic: The first schools founded in this period were accordingly the Tongwen Guan in Beijing, the Guangfangyan Guan in Shanghai, the Fujian Naval Administration School, and the naval and military academies of the Northern and Southern Fleets.

sentences.zh: 京師同文館之設，從總理各國事務衙門之請，始於同治元年。

translations.literal: The establishment of the capital Tongwen Guan, at the request of the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs, began in the first year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Beijing Tongwen Guan was established in 1862 at the request of the Zongli Yamen (Office for the Management of Foreign Affairs).

sentences.zh: 初止教授各國語言文字。

translations.literal: At first it only taught the languages and scripts of various countries.
translations.idiomatic: At first it taught only foreign languages and scripts.

sentences.zh: 六年，議於同文館內添設算學館。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, it was proposed to add a mathematics school within the Tongwen Guan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 it was proposed to add a school of mathematics within the Tongwen Guan.

sentences.zh: 時京僚瞢於時務，謗讟繁興，原疏排斥眾議，言之剴切。

translations.literal: At the time Beijing officials were blind to current affairs; slander flourished, but the original memorial rejected the multitude of opinions and spoke with penetrating force.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials were then ignorant of current affairs, and criticism was widespread; the original memorial rebutted these views in forceful, pointed language.

sentences.zh: 謂：「西人制器之法，無不由度數而生。

translations.literal: It stated: "The Westerners' methods of making implements all arise from measurement and number.
translations.idiomatic: It argued: "Western methods of manufacturing all derive from mathematics.

sentences.zh: 中國欲講求製造輪船、機器諸法，苟不藉西士為先導，師心自用，無裨實際。

translations.literal: If China wishes to study the methods of building steamships and machinery, and does not rely on Westerners as guides but follows its own conceits, it will be of no practical benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If China wishes to master the building of steamships and machinery, it cannot do without Western teachers as guides; to follow one's own conceits alone will accomplish nothing in practice.

sentences.zh: 疆臣如左宗棠、李鴻章等，皆深明其理，堅持其說，詳於奏牘。

translations.literal: Frontier officials such as Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang all deeply understood this principle, firmly upheld this view, and set it forth in detail in their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier governors such as Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang all understood this principle well, held firmly to it, and argued it at length in their memorials.

sentences.zh: 且西人之術，聖祖深韙之矣，當時列在台官，垂為時憲，本朝掌故，不宜數典而忘。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Sage Emperor deeply approved of Western techniques; they were then listed among the officials of the Astronomical Bureau and handed down as standards of the age—dynastic precedents of our court that one should not cite the classics and forget.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Kangxi Emperor had deeply approved of Western learning; it was recorded among the Astronomical Bureau's duties and handed down as a standard of the age—precedents of our dynasty that must not be forgotten while citing the classics.

sentences.zh: 若以師法西人為恥，其說尤謬。

translations.literal: If one takes learning from Westerners as shameful, that view is especially absurd.
translations.idiomatic: To regard learning from the West as shameful is an especially absurd notion.

sentences.zh: 中國狃於因循，不思振作，恥孰甚焉。

translations.literal: China clings to routine and does not think of rousing itself—what shame could be greater?
translations.idiomatic: For China to cling to old ways and refuse to rouse itself—what shame could be greater?

sentences.zh: 今不以不如人為恥，獨以學其人為恥，將安於不如而終不學，遂可雪恥乎？

translations.literal: Now if one is not ashamed of being inferior to others, yet is ashamed only of learning from them, and will rest content in inferiority and never learn—can shame then be wiped away?
translations.idiomatic: If we are not ashamed of being inferior yet are ashamed of learning from those who surpass us, and prefer to remain inferior rather than study—how can that ever restore our honor?

sentences.zh: 學期適用，事貴因時，物議雖多，權衡宜定。

translations.literal: The term of study should suit practical needs; affairs value adapting to the times; though public talk is abundant, the balance ought to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: The course of study must suit practical needs, and policy must adapt to the times; though criticism abounds, a firm decision is required.

sentences.zh: 原議招取滿、漢舉人，恩、拔、副、歲、優貢生，並由此出身之正途人員。

translations.literal: The original proposal was to recruit Manchu and Han juren, enshi, bajian, fujian, sui, and you gongsheng, and regular-path personnel of such origins.
translations.idiomatic: The original plan was to recruit Manchu and Han juren, enshi, bajian, fujian, sui, and you gongsheng, and other officials who had entered by the regular examination route.

sentences.zh: 又擬推廣，凡翰林院庶吉士、編修、檢討，與五品以下進士出身之京、外各官，年在三十歲以內者，均可送考。

translations.literal: It was further proposed to extend recruitment: all Hanlin bachelors, compilers, and revisers, and capital and provincial officials of fifth rank and below who were jinshi, under thirty years of age, might be sent to sit for examination.
translations.idiomatic: It was further proposed that Hanlin bachelors, compilers, and revisers, and capital and provincial officials of fifth rank and below who were jinshi and under thirty, might all be sent to enroll.

sentences.zh: 三年考列高等者，按升階優保班次，以示鼓勵。

translations.literal: Those ranked high after three years of examination would be advanced in grade and given preferential promotion quotas as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, those who ranked highest would receive preferential promotion in grade and quota as encouragement.

sentences.zh: 」詔從其議。

translations.literal: " An edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 上海廣方言館，創設於同治二年。

translations.literal: The Shanghai Guangfangyan Guan was founded in the second year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanghai Guangfangyan Guan was founded in 1863.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫李鴻章言：「京師同文館之設，實為良法。

translations.literal: Jiangsu governor Li Hongzhang stated: "The establishment of the capital Tongwen Guan is truly a good method.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu governor Li Hongzhang wrote: "The founding of the Beijing Tongwen Guan is truly an excellent model.

sentences.zh: 惟洋人總匯地，以上海、廣東兩口為最。

translations.literal: Only the places where foreigners chiefly gather are greatest at Shanghai and Guangdong ports.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the chief centers where foreigners congregate are the ports of Shanghai and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 擬仿照同文館例，於上海添設外國語言文字學館，選近郡年十四歲以下資稟穎悟、根器端靜之文童，聘西人教習，並聘內地品學兼優之舉、貢生員，課以經、史、文藝。

translations.literal: It is proposed to follow the Tongwen Guan precedent and add in Shanghai a school of foreign languages and scripts, selecting from nearby prefectures literary youths under fourteen, of keen talent and steady character, employing Westerners to teach, and also hiring from the interior juren and gongsheng of excellent character and learning to instruct them in the classics, history, and belles-lettres.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed to follow the Tongwen Guan model and establish in Shanghai a school of foreign languages, selecting bright, well-mannered boys under fourteen from nearby prefectures, hiring Westerners to instruct them and accomplished juren and gongsheng from inland to teach the classics, history, and literature.

sentences.zh: 學成送本省督、撫考驗，作為該縣附學生。

translations.literal: When their studies were complete they would be sent to the provincial governor-general and governor for examination and registered as supplementary students of their counties.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completion they would be examined by the provincial governor and registered as county supplementary students.

sentences.zh: 其候補、佐雜等官，年少聰慧者，許入館一體學習，學成酌給升途。

translations.literal: Expectant appointees and subordinate officials who were young and clever might also be permitted to study in the school together; upon completion advancement would be granted as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Young, able expectant and subordinate officials might also enroll; upon graduation they would receive appropriate advancement.

sentences.zh: 三五年後，有此一種讀書明理之人，精通番語，凡通商、督、撫衙署及海關監督，應設繙譯官承辦洋務者，即於館中遴選派充。

translations.literal: In three to five years, with this kind of educated, reasonable men proficient in foreign languages, wherever treaty ports, governor-general and governor yamens, and customs superintendencies required translators to handle foreign affairs, they could be selected and appointed from the school.
translations.idiomatic: Within three to five years there would be educated men fluent in foreign languages, and wherever treaty ports, provincial offices, or customs posts needed translators for foreign affairs, they could be chosen from the school.

sentences.zh: 庶關稅、軍需可期核實；

translations.literal: Thus customs revenue and military supplies might be expected to be verified accurately;
translations.idiomatic: Customs revenue and military supplies could then be verified accurately;

sentences.zh: 無賴通事，亦稍斂跡。

translations.literal: and rascally interpreters would also somewhat restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: and unscrupulous interpreters would be somewhat checked.

sentences.zh: 且能盡閱西人未譯專書，探賾索隱，一切輪船、火器等巧技，由漸通曉，於自強之道，不無裨助。

translations.literal: Moreover they could read through Western specialist books not yet translated, probe the profound and seek the hidden; all the ingenious skills of steamships, firearms, and the like would gradually become understood, which would not be without help on the path of self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: They could also read untranslated Western technical works, probe their depths, and gradually master the skills of steamships, firearms, and the like—no small aid to self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 」上諭廣州將軍查照辦理。

translations.literal: " The throne instructed the Guangzhou general to investigate and act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne ordered the Guangzhou general to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 福建船廠，同治五年，左宗棠督閩時奏設，並設隨廠學堂。

translations.literal: The Fujian shipyard was memorialized for establishment in the fifth year of Tongzhi when Zuo Zongtang supervised Fujian, and a school attached to the yard was also set up.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian shipyard was established in 1866 while Zuo Zongtang governed Fujian, together with an attached school.

sentences.zh: 分前、後二堂。

translations.literal: It was divided into front and rear halls.
translations.idiomatic: The school was divided into front and rear halls.

sentences.zh: 前堂習法文，練習造船之術；

translations.literal: The front hall studied French and practiced shipbuilding;
translations.idiomatic: The front hall studied French and shipbuilding;

sentences.zh: 後堂習英文，練習駕駛之術。

translations.literal: the rear hall studied English and practiced navigation.
translations.idiomatic: the rear hall studied English and navigation.

sentences.zh: 課程除造船、駕駛應習常課外，兼習策論，令讀聖諭廣訓、孝經以明義理。

translations.literal: Beyond the regular courses in shipbuilding and navigation, the curriculum also included policy essays, and students were made to read the Sacred Edict and the Classic of Filial Piety to clarify moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the required courses in shipbuilding and navigation, students also wrote policy essays and read the Sacred Edict and the Classic of Filial Piety to ground themselves in moral principle.

sentences.zh: 首總船政者為沈葆楨，規畫閎遠，尤重視學堂。

translations.literal: The first director of naval administration was Shen Baozhen, whose planning was broad and far-reaching and who especially valued the school.
translations.idiomatic: The first director-general of the shipyard was Shen Baozhen, whose plans were ambitious and who placed special emphasis on the school.

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏陳船工善後事宜：「請選派前、後堂生分赴英、法，學習製造駕駛之方，及推陳出新、練兵制勝之理。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized on follow-up matters for shipbuilding: "It is requested to select and dispatch students of the front and rear halls separately to Britain and France to learn methods of manufacture and navigation, and the principles of innovation, troop training, and gaining victory.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 he memorialized on the shipyard's follow-up work: "Students from the front and rear halls should be sent to Britain and France to learn shipbuilding and navigation, and the principles of innovation, military training, and victory in war.

sentences.zh: 學生有天資傑出，能習礦學、化學及交涉、公法等事，均可隨宜肄業。

translations.literal: Students of outstanding natural talent who could study mining, chemistry, diplomacy, international law, and the like might all pursue studies as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Students of outstanding ability might also study mining, chemistry, diplomacy, international law, and related subjects as suited their gifts.

sentences.zh: 」尋葆楨任南洋大臣。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward Shen Baozhen took office as Southern Seas minister.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Baozhen was soon appointed minister for the Southern Seas.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，奏派華、洋監督，訂定章程。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he memorialized to appoint Chinese and foreign superintendents and fix regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he memorialized for the appointment of Chinese and foreign superintendents and the drafting of regulations.

sentences.zh: 船政學堂成就之人材，實為中國海軍人材之嚆矢。

translations.literal: The talent produced by the Naval Administration School was in truth the first arrow of China's naval personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The talent trained at the Naval Administration School were in truth the pioneers of China's modern navy.

sentences.zh: 學堂設於馬尾，故清季海軍將領，亦以閩人為最多。

translations.literal: Because the school was located at Mawei, late Qing naval commanders were also mostly men of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Because the school stood at Mawei, late Qing naval officers were predominantly Fujianese.

sentences.zh: 天津水師學堂，光緒八年，北洋大臣李鴻章奏設。

translations.literal: The Tianjin Naval Academy was memorialized for establishment in the eighth year of Guangxu by Beiyang minister Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin Naval Academy was established in 1882 on Li Hongzhang's memorial as Beiyang minister.

sentences.zh: 次年招取學生，入堂肄業。

translations.literal: The next year students were recruited to enter and study in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: The following year students were recruited and enrolled.

sentences.zh: 分駕駛、管輪兩科。

translations.literal: It was divided into navigation and engineering departments.
translations.idiomatic: It had two branches: navigation and marine engineering.

sentences.zh: 教授用英文，兼習操法，及讀經、國文等科。

translations.literal: Instruction was in English, with drill methods also studied, and reading of the classics and national literature.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction was in English, together with drill, the classics, and Chinese composition.

sentences.zh: 優者遣派出洋留學，以資深造。

translations.literal: Outstanding students were sent abroad to study for further training.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding students were sent abroad for advanced study.

sentences.zh: 厥後海軍諸將帥由此畢業者甚夥。

translations.literal: Thereafter very many naval commanders graduated from it.
translations.idiomatic: Many later naval commanders were graduates of this academy.

sentences.zh: 鴻章又於光緒十一年奏設天津武備學堂，規制略仿西國陸軍學堂。

translations.literal: Hongzhang again memorialized in the eleventh year of Guangxu to establish the Tianjin Military Academy, its regulations broadly modeled on Western army schools.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang also memorialized in 1885 for the Tianjin Military Academy, modeled broadly on Western army schools.

sentences.zh: 挑選營中精健聰穎、略通文義之弁目，入堂肄業。

translations.literal: Sturdy, clever sergeants in the camps who had some grasp of letters were selected to enter and study.
translations.idiomatic: Able, literate sergeants from the camps were selected for enrollment.

sentences.zh: 文員原習武事者，一併錄取。

translations.literal: Civilian officials who had originally studied military affairs were also admitted together.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian officials with military training were admitted as well.

sentences.zh: 其課程一面研究西洋行軍新法，如後膛各種槍砲，土木營壘及布陣分合攻守各術。

translations.literal: The curriculum on one hand studied Western new methods of campaigning, such as breech-loading guns of various kinds, field fortifications, and the techniques of deploying formations, dividing and combining, attacking and defending.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum covered Western campaigning methods—breech-loading arms, fieldworks, and the tactics of deployment, maneuver, attack, and defense.

sentences.zh: 一面赴營實習，演試槍砲陣勢及造築台壘。

translations.literal: On the other hand they went to camp for practical training, drilling with firearms and formations and constructing batteries and fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Students also trained in camp, drilling with firearms and formations and building batteries and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 惟學生系挑選弁目，雖聘用德國教員，不能直接聽講，仍用繙譯，展轉教授，與水師學堂注重外國文者不同。

translations.literal: Only because the students were selected sergeants, though German instructors were hired, they could not listen directly to lectures; instruction still passed through translators in relay, unlike the naval academy which emphasized foreign languages.
translations.idiomatic: Because the students were sergeants, however, even with German instructors they could not follow lectures directly; teaching still went through interpreters—unlike the naval academy, which stressed foreign languages.

sentences.zh: 初制，學習一年後，考試及格學生，發回各營，由統領量材授事。

translations.literal: Under the original system, after one year of study, students who passed examination were sent back to their camps, and commanders assigned duties according to their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, after one year, passing students returned to their units for commanders to assign duties according to ability.

sentences.zh: 其後逐漸延長年限，選募良家年幼子弟肄業。

translations.literal: Later the term was gradually extended, and sons of respectable families were recruited while young to study.
translations.idiomatic: Later the course was lengthened and sons of respectable families were recruited while young.

sentences.zh: 迨庚子之變，學堂適當戰區，全校淪為灰燼矣。

translations.literal: When the Gengzi upheaval came, the academy happened to lie in the war zone, and the entire school was reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Boxer uprising of 1900 the academy lay in the war zone and was burned to the ground.

sentences.zh: 此外廣東水陸師學堂，則粵督張之洞於光緒十三年奏設。

translations.literal: Besides these, the Guangdong naval and military academy was memorialized for establishment in the thirteenth year of Guangxu by Guangdong governor Zhang Zhidong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong's combined naval and military academy was also established in 1887 on Zhang Zhidong's memorial as governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 之洞調任鄂督，二十一年又奏設湖北武備學堂，其辦法課程，水師分管輪、駕駛兩項，陸師分馬、步，槍、砲，營造等項，大略參照北洋成法。

translations.literal: When Zhidong was transferred to Hubei governor, in the twenty-first year he again memorialized to establish the Hubei Military Academy; its methods and curriculum divided the naval branch into engineering and navigation, and the land branch into cavalry, infantry, musketry, artillery, construction, and the like, broadly following Beiyang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hubei, he memorialized in 1895 for the Hubei Military Academy, with naval branches in engineering and navigation and land branches in cavalry, infantry, firearms, artillery, and construction—broadly following the Beiyang model.

sentences.zh: 洎海軍成立，新軍改建，此類學堂，南洋及各省增設日盛，不具述。

translations.literal: By the time the navy was formed and the new army reorganized, such academies multiplied daily in the Southern Seas region and the provinces; they are not described in detail here.
translations.idiomatic: Once the navy was organized and the new army reformed, such schools proliferated in the south and the provinces; they are not described here in detail.

sentences.zh: 至湖北自強學堂，亦之洞創設。

translations.literal: As for the Hubei Self-Strengthening Academy, it too was founded by Zhidong.
translations.idiomatic: The Hubei Self-Strengthening Academy was also Zhang Zhidong's creation.

sentences.zh: 初分方言、格致、算學、商務四門。

translations.literal: At first it was divided into four departments: foreign languages, natural science, mathematics, and commerce.
translations.idiomatic: It was first divided into four departments: foreign languages, natural science, mathematics, and commerce.

sentences.zh: 惟方言一齋，住堂肄業，餘三齋按月考課。

translations.literal: Only the foreign-language hall had resident students; the other three halls were examined monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Only the language department had resident students; the other three held monthly examinations.

sentences.zh: 其後算學改歸兩湖書院教授，格致、商務停課，本堂專課方言，以為西學梯階。

translations.literal: Later mathematics was transferred to instruction at the Two Lakes Academy; natural science and commerce ceased classes, and the main academy devoted itself solely to foreign languages as a ladder to Western learning.
translations.idiomatic: Later mathematics was taught at the Two Lakes Academy, natural science and commerce were dropped, and the academy devoted itself solely to languages as a gateway to Western learning.

sentences.zh: 方言分英、法、德、俄四門，亦類似同文館之學堂也。

translations.literal: Foreign languages were divided into English, French, German, and Russian—a school also similar to the Tongwen Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Languages were taught in English, French, German, and Russian—a school much like the Tongwen Guan.

sentences.zh: 光緒丙申、丁酉間，各省學堂未能普設，中外臣工多以變通整頓書院為請。

translations.literal: Between the bingshen and dingyou years of Guangxu, as academies could not be universally established in the provinces, Chinese and foreign officials often petitioned to adapt and reorganize the traditional academies.
translations.idiomatic: Around 1896–1897, when modern schools could not yet be established everywhere, officials repeatedly petitioned to reform the traditional academies instead.

sentences.zh: 詔飭裁改，禮部議准章程，並課天算、格致等學。

translations.literal: An edict ordered their restructuring; the Board of Rites approved regulations and also made astronomy, mathematics, and natural science subjects of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their restructuring; the Board of Rites approved regulations requiring instruction in astronomy, mathematics, and natural science.

sentences.zh: 陝西等省創設格致實學書院，以補學堂之不逮焉。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and other provinces founded academies of practical natural science to supplement what the new schools could not yet provide.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and other provinces founded academies of practical science to fill gaps the new schools could not yet meet.

sentences.zh: 齋大抵此期設學之宗旨，專註重實用。

translations.literal: Roughly speaking, the purpose of establishing schools in this period focused exclusively on practical utility.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly speaking, the aim of schooling in this period was overwhelmingly practical.

sentences.zh: 蓋其動機緣於對外，故外國語及海陸軍得此期教育之主要，無學制系統之足言。

translations.literal: Because its motive arose from foreign relations, foreign languages and naval and military affairs became the main substance of education in this period; there was scarcely a school system worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Because the impulse came from foreign pressure, foreign languages and naval and military training dominated this period's education; there was as yet no real school system to speak of.

sentences.zh: 惟南洋公學雖亦承襲此期教育之宗旨，而學制分為三等，已寓普通學校及豫備教育之意旨。

translations.literal: Only the Nanyang Public School, though it also inherited this period's educational purpose, divided its system into three grades and already embodied the idea of common schools and preparatory education.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang Public School alone, while sharing this period's practical emphasis, divided instruction into three grades and already embodied the ideas of general and preparatory education.

sentences.zh: 先是光緒二十一年，津海關道盛宣懷於天津創設頭、二等學堂。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the twenty-first year of Guangxu, Tianjin customs intendant Sheng Xuanhuai founded first- and second-grade schools in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895 Tianjin customs intendant Sheng Xuanhuai had founded first- and second-grade schools in Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 頭等學堂課程四年，等一年習竣，欲專習一門者，得察學生資質酌定。

translations.literal: The first-grade school had a four-year course; after one year of general study, those wishing to specialize in one field might have their specialization determined according to the student's aptitude.
translations.idiomatic: The first-grade school offered a four-year course; after one year of general study, specialization could be chosen according to each student's aptitude.

sentences.zh: 專門凡五：一工程學，二電學，三礦務學，四機器學，五律例學。

translations.literal: Specializations numbered five: first engineering, second electricity, third mining, fourth machinery, fifth law.
translations.idiomatic: There were five specializations: engineering, electrical science, mining, machinery, and law.

sentences.zh: 二等學堂課程四年，按班次遞升，習滿升入頭等。

translations.literal: The second-grade school had a four-year course, advancing by class year, and upon completion students rose to the first grade.
translations.idiomatic: The second-grade school also ran four years, with promotion by class; graduates advanced to the first grade.

sentences.zh: 意謂二等擬外國小學，頭等擬外國大學。

translations.literal: The intent was that the second grade corresponded to foreign primary schools and the first grade to foreign universities.
translations.idiomatic: The second grade was conceived as equivalent to a Western primary school, the first grade to a university.

sentences.zh: 因初設，采通融求速辦法。

translations.literal: Because it was newly founded, flexible methods were adopted to achieve rapid establishment.
translations.idiomatic: As a new venture, flexible shortcuts were adopted to launch quickly.

sentences.zh: 教員既苦乏才，學生亦難精擇，無甚成效。

translations.literal: Teachers were sorely lacking in talent, and students were hard to select with care; there was little achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Qualified teachers were scarce and students hard to select carefully; little was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，宣懷又於上海創設南洋公學，如津學制而損益之，經費取給招商、電報兩局捐助。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Xuanhuai again founded the Nanyang Public School in Shanghai, adapting the Tianjin system with modifications; funds were drawn from donations by the China Merchants Steam Navigation and Telegraph bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 Sheng Xuanhuai founded the Nanyang Public School in Shanghai, adapting the Tianjin model; its funds came from the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company and the Telegraph Administration.

sentences.zh: 奏明辦理，因名公學。

translations.literal: He memorialized for approval to operate it, and it was therefore named a public school.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for imperial approval and named it a public school (gongxue).

sentences.zh: 分四院：曰師範院，曰外院，曰中院，曰上院。

translations.literal: It was divided into four colleges: Normal, Outer, Middle, and Upper.
translations.idiomatic: It was divided into four colleges: Normal, Primary (Outer), Middle, and Upper.

sentences.zh: 外院即附屬小學，為師範生練習之所。

translations.literal: The Outer college was the attached primary school, a place for normal students to practice.
translations.idiomatic: The Outer college was the attached primary school where normal students practiced teaching.

sentences.zh: 中、上院即二等、頭等學堂，寓中學堂、高等學堂之意。

translations.literal: The Middle and Upper colleges were the second- and first-grade schools, embodying the ideas of middle and higher schools.
translations.idiomatic: The Middle and Upper colleges corresponded to the second- and first-grade schools—the equivalents of middle and higher schools.

sentences.zh: 課程大體分中文、英文兩部，而注重法政、經濟。

translations.literal: The curriculum was broadly divided into Chinese and English sections, with emphasis on law, government, and economics.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum was divided chiefly between Chinese and English, with emphasis on law, government, and economics.

sentences.zh: 上院畢業生，擇尤異者咨送出洋，就學於各國大學。

translations.literal: Graduates of the Upper college who were especially outstanding were memorialized and sent abroad to study at universities in various countries.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding Upper college graduates were recommended and sent abroad to attend foreign universities.

sentences.zh: 意謂內國大學猝難設置，以公學為豫備學校，而以外國大學為最高學府。

translations.literal: The intent was that domestic universities could not quickly be established; the public school would serve as preparatory school, and foreign universities as the highest academies.
translations.idiomatic: The idea was that national universities could not be set up overnight; the public school would serve as preparatory school and foreign universities as the summit of learning.

sentences.zh: 論者謂中國教育有系統之組織，此其見端焉。

translations.literal: Commentators say that China's education acquired systematic organization—this was its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators regard this as the first sign of a systematic organization of education in China.

sentences.zh: 後改歸郵傳部管轄，定名高等實業學堂。

translations.literal: Later it was transferred to the Ministry of Posts and Communications and given the fixed name Higher Practical School.
translations.idiomatic: Later it passed to the Ministry of Posts and Communications and was renamed the Higher Practical School.

sentences.zh: 其課程性質，非復設立之初旨。

translations.literal: The character of its curriculum no longer matched the purpose at founding.
translations.idiomatic: Its curriculum no longer reflected its original purpose.

sentences.zh: 此第一期無系統教育之大略也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline of the first period of unsystematic education.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the first period of education without a unified system.

sentences.zh: 自甲午一役，喪師辱國，列強群起，攘奪權利，國勢益岌岌。

translations.literal: Since the single battle of Jiawu, with armies lost and the nation shamed, the great powers rose together to seize rights, and the national situation grew ever more perilous.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of 1894–95, with armies lost and national honor shattered, the powers scrambled for concessions and the state's position grew ever more desperate.

sentences.zh: 朝野志士，恍然於鄉者變法之不得其本。

translations.literal: Court and country men of purpose suddenly realized that the reform of earlier days had not grasped the root.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and reformers alike suddenly saw that earlier reforms had missed the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李端棻、主事康有為等，均條議推廣學堂。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Duanfen, Clerk Kang Youwei, and others all submitted detailed proposals to expand schools.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Duanfen, Clerk Kang Youwei, and others all submitted detailed plans to expand schooling.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，德宗諭曰：「邇者詔書數下，開特科，改武科制度，立大、小學堂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, the Guangxu Emperor instructed: "Recently edicts have been issued repeatedly, opening special examinations, reforming the military examination system, and establishing great and small schools.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 the Guangxu Emperor decreed: "Edicts have lately been issued again and again—opening special examinations, reforming the military examination system, and founding universities and schools.

sentences.zh: 惟風氣尚未大開，論說莫衷一是。

translations.literal: Only the prevailing mood has not yet greatly opened; discussions do not reach a single conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet public sentiment has not fully shifted, and opinion remains divided.

sentences.zh: 國是不定，則號令不行。

translations.literal: If the national policy is not fixed, then orders cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Without a settled national policy, no decree can be enforced.

sentences.zh: 特明白宣示中外，自王公至士庶，各宜努力發憤，以聖賢義理之學植其根本，博採西學切於時務者，實力講求，以救空疏迂謬之弊。

translations.literal: It is specially and clearly proclaimed to China and abroad that from princes and dukes to commoners, each should strive to rouse himself, plant his roots in the learning of sages and worthies in moral principle, and earnestly study Western learning relevant to current affairs, to remedy the defects of emptiness, superficiality, and absurdity.
translations.idiomatic: The throne therefore proclaimed to all, from princes to commoners, that each should strive to master the moral teachings of the sages while earnestly studying Western learning useful for present needs, so as to cure the ills of empty pedantry and absurdity.

sentences.zh: 京師大學為各省倡，應首先舉辦。

translations.literal: The Imperial University in the capital should lead the provinces and be established first.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University in the capital should lead the provinces and be founded first.

sentences.zh: 凡翰林編、檢，部、院司員，各門侍衛，候補、候選道，府、州、縣以下各官，大員子弟，八旗世職，各省武職後裔，均准入學肄業，以期人材輩出，共濟時艱。

translations.literal: All Hanlin compilers and revisers, ministry and yamen clerks, gate guards of every corps, expectant and candidate circuit intendants, officials from prefectures, departments, and counties downward, sons of high officials, hereditary Banner offices, and descendants of provincial military officials in every province may all be admitted to study, in hope that talent will emerge in succession to meet the urgent crisis of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin compilers and revisers, ministry and yamen clerks, guards, expectant officials, local magistrates, sons of high officials, Banner hereditary officers, and military descendants nationwide were all to be admitted, so that talent might emerge to meet the national crisis.

sentences.zh: 」下軍機大臣、總理各國事務王、大臣，妥議奏聞。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Grand Council and the princes and ministers in charge of foreign affairs to deliberate carefully and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was referred to the Grand Council and the Zongli Yamen for deliberation and memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋議覆籌辦京師大學堂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they memorialized in reply on planning the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: They soon memorialized on organizing the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 擬定章程，要端凡四：一寬籌經費，二宏建學舍，三慎選管學大臣，四簡派總教習。

translations.literal: Regulations were drafted; the main points numbered four: first, broadly provide funds; second, greatly build school buildings; third, carefully select the superintendent of studies; fourth, appoint a chief instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Draft regulations set forth four essentials: secure ample funding, expand buildings, choose a superintendent of studies with care, and appoint a chief instructor.

sentences.zh: 詔如所擬。

translations.literal: An edict approved the proposal as drafted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 命孫家鼐管理大學堂事務，經費由戶部籌撥。

translations.literal: Sun Jianai was ordered to manage Imperial University affairs; funds were to be allocated from the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jianai was appointed to manage the university; the Board of Revenue was to supply funds.

sentences.zh: 五月，又諭各直省督、撫，將各省府、廳、州、縣大、小書院，一律改為兼習中、西學之學校，其階級，以省會之大書院為高等學，郡城之書院為中學，州、縣之書院為小學。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, another edict instructed every provincial governor-general and governor to convert all great and small academies in prefectures, departments, states, and counties into schools teaching both Chinese and Western learning; the grades were: provincial capital great academies as higher schools, prefectural academies as middle schools, and departmental and county academies as primary schools.
translations.idiomatic: In May another edict ordered every governor to convert all provincial, prefectural, and county academies into schools teaching both Chinese and Western learning—provincial academies as higher schools, prefectural as middle schools, and county as primary schools.

sentences.zh: 頒給京師大學章程，令仿照辦理。

translations.literal: The regulations of the Imperial University were issued for imitation in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University regulations were issued as a model.

sentences.zh: 各書院經費，侭數提作學堂經費。

translations.literal: All academy funds were to be fully transferred as school funds.
translations.idiomatic: All academy endowments were to be transferred entirely to the schools.

sentences.zh: 紳民如能捐建學堂，或廣為勸募，准奏請給獎。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners who could donate schools or widely solicit contributions might memorialize for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry who built schools or raised funds might petition for rewards.

sentences.zh: 有獨立措捐鉅款者，予以破格之賞。

translations.literal: Those who independently raised large sums were to receive exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: Those who raised large sums on their own were to receive exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 民間祠廟不在祀典者，一律改為學堂，以節糜費而隆教育。

translations.literal: Popular temples not in the official sacrificial canon were all to be converted to schools, to save waste and elevate education.
translations.idiomatic: Folk temples not on the official register were to become schools, to save waste and promote education.

sentences.zh: 是時管學大臣之權限，不專管理京師大學堂，並節制各省所設之學堂。

translations.literal: At that time the superintendent of studies' authority was not limited to managing the Imperial University but also controlled schools established in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent's authority extended beyond the Imperial University to all provincial schools.

sentences.zh: 實以大學校長兼全國教育部長之職權。

translations.literal: In reality he held the powers of a university president combined with a national minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: In effect he combined the roles of university president and national minister of education.

sentences.zh: 又以同文館及北洋學堂多以西人為總教習，於中學不免偏枯。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the Tongwen Guan and Beiyang academies mostly took Westerners as chief instructors, Chinese learning was inevitably one-sided.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Tongwen Guan and Beiyang schools chiefly employed Westerners as head teachers, Chinese learning was inevitably neglected.

sentences.zh: 且外國文不止一國，學科各有專門，非一西人所能勝任。

translations.literal: Moreover, foreign languages are not limited to one country, and subjects each have specialists; no single Westerner can fill all roles.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign languages are many, and each subject requires specialists; no one Westerner could cover them all.

sentences.zh: 必擇學貫中、西，能見其大之中國學者，為總教習，破格錄用，有選派分教習之權。

translations.literal: One must choose a Chinese scholar thoroughly versed in both China and the West who can see the larger picture as chief instructor, appointed exceptionally, with authority to select and assign assistant instructors.
translations.idiomatic: A Chinese scholar thoroughly versed in both traditions who grasped the larger picture had to serve as chief instructor, appointed by exception with power to choose assistants.

sentences.zh: 蓋以管學大臣必大學士或尚書充任，而總教習則不拘資格，可延攬新進之人才也。

translations.literal: This was because the superintendent of studies had to be a grand secretary or minister, while the chief instructor was not bound by rank and could recruit rising talent.
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent had to be a grand secretary or minister, but the chief instructor was not bound by rank and could recruit rising talent.

sentences.zh: 學生分兩班，已治普通學卒業者為頭班，現治普通學者為二班，猶是南洋公學之舊法。

translations.literal: Students were divided into two classes: the first class were those who had completed general studies; the second were those presently studying general studies—still the old method of the Nanyang Public School.
translations.idiomatic: Students were divided into two classes: those who had finished general studies formed the first class; those still in general studies formed the second—the old Nanyang Public School arrangement.

sentences.zh: 課程分普通、專門兩類。

translations.literal: Courses were divided into general and specialized categories.
translations.idiomatic: Courses fell into general and specialized categories.

sentences.zh: 普通學，學生必須通習；

translations.literal: In general studies, students must master all subjects;
translations.idiomatic: General studies were compulsory for all;

sentences.zh: 專門學，人各佔一門或二門。

translations.literal: in specialized studies, each person took one or two subjects.
translations.idiomatic: specialized studies allowed one or two subjects per student.

sentences.zh: 普通學科目為經學，理學，掌故學，諸子學，初級算學，初級格致學，初級政治學，初級地理學，文學，體操學，語言文字學。

translations.literal: General subjects were classical studies, Neo-Confucian philosophy, institutional history, masters' learning, elementary mathematics, elementary natural science, elementary political science, elementary geography, belles-lettres, gymnastics, and languages and scripts.
translations.idiomatic: General subjects included the classics, Neo-Confucian philosophy, institutional history, masters' texts, elementary mathematics, natural science, political science, geography, literature, gymnastics, and languages.

sentences.zh: 專門學科目為高等算學，高等格致學，高等政治學、法律屬之，高等地理學、測繪屬之，農學，礦學，工程學，商學，兵學，衛生學、醫學屬之。

translations.literal: Specialized subjects were higher mathematics, higher natural science, higher political science including law, higher geography including surveying, agriculture, mining, engineering, commerce, military science, and hygiene including medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Specialized subjects included advanced mathematics, natural science, political science and law, geography and surveying, agriculture, mining, engineering, commerce, military science, and hygiene and medicine.

sentences.zh: 考驗學生，用積分法。

translations.literal: Students were examined by the point-accumulation method.
translations.idiomatic: Student progress was tracked by a points system.

sentences.zh: 學生月給膏火銀兩有差。

translations.literal: Students received monthly stipends of silver in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Students received monthly stipends in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 上海設編譯局，各學科除外國文外，均讀編譯課本。

translations.literal: A translation bureau was set up in Shanghai; except for foreign languages, all subjects read translated textbooks.
translations.idiomatic: A translation bureau was established in Shanghai; except foreign languages, all subjects used translated textbooks.

sentences.zh: 籌辦大學章程之概要如此。

translations.literal: Such was the general outline of the regulations for establishing the university.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general outline of the university regulations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，八月政變，由舊黨把持朝局，卒釀成庚子之禍。

translations.literal: Before long, in the eighth-month coup conservatives seized the court and ultimately brought on the Gengzi disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the coup of September 1898 put conservatives in control and ultimately led to the Boxer catastrophe of 1900.

sentences.zh: 逮二十七年，學校漸有復興之議。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year, discussion of gradually reviving schools arose.
translations.idiomatic: By 1901 discussion of reviving the schools had begun.

sentences.zh: 其首倡者，則山東巡撫袁世凱也。

translations.literal: The first to advocate it was Shandong governor Yuan Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: The first advocate was Shandong governor Yuan Shikai.

sentences.zh: 初，世凱奏陳東省開辦大學堂章程，有旨飭下各省仿辦，令政務處會同禮部妥議選舉鼓勵章程。

translations.literal: Initially Yuan memorialized regulations for establishing a university in Shandong; an edict ordered provinces to follow the model and directed the Office of Government Affairs together with the Board of Rites to deliberate regulations for selection and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had memorialized regulations for a Shandong university; the throne ordered provinces to follow suit and directed the Office of Government Affairs and Board of Rites to draft selection and incentive regulations.

sentences.zh: 尋議言：「東西各國學堂，皆系小學、中學、大學以次遞升，畢業後始予出身，擬請按照辦理。

translations.literal: Soon the deliberation stated: "Schools in East and West all advance step by step from primary through middle to university, granting office only after graduation; it is proposed to follow this method.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation stated: "Western schools advance from primary through middle to university and grant office only after graduation; we propose to follow this.

sentences.zh: 小學畢業生考試合格，選入中學堂。

translations.literal: Primary graduates who pass examination are selected into middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: Primary graduates who pass examination enter middle school.

sentences.zh: 畢業考試合格，再選入大學堂。

translations.literal: Upon passing graduation examination, they are again selected into the university.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-school graduates who pass enter the university.

sentences.zh: 畢業考試合格，發給憑照。

translations.literal: Upon passing graduation examination, credentials are issued.
translations.idiomatic: University graduates receive credentials.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、學政，按其功課，嚴密扃試。

translations.literal: Governors-general, governors, and education commissioners, according to their coursework, conduct rigorous sealed examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial authorities conduct rigorous sealed examinations according to coursework.

sentences.zh: 優者分別等第，咨送京師大學堂覆試，作為舉人、貢生。

translations.literal: The outstanding are graded by rank and referred to the Imperial University for re-examination, qualifying as juren or gongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The best are graded and sent to the Imperial University for re-examination as juren or gongsheng.

sentences.zh: 其貢生留下屆應考，原應鄉試者聽。

translations.literal: Gongsheng remain for the next examination cycle; those originally eligible for the provincial examination may still take it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsheng wait for the next cycle; those eligible for the provincial examination may still take it.

sentences.zh: 舉人積有成數，由京師大學堂嚴加考試，優者分別等第，咨送禮部。

translations.literal: When juren accumulate in sufficient number, the Imperial University conducts rigorous examination; the outstanding are graded by rank and referred to the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When enough juren accumulate, the Imperial University examines them strictly and refers the best to the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 簡派大臣考試，候旨欽定，作為進士，一體殿試，酌加擢用，優予官階。

translations.literal: Ministers are specially dispatched to examine them; after imperial confirmation they qualify as jinshi, all take the palace examination, and advancement and rank are granted as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioners examine them; the throne names them jinshi, they take the palace examination, and ranks are assigned accordingly.

translations.idiomatic: Yuan's plan, because schools could not be built everywhere at once, began with a provincial school whose preparatory and main halls embodied primary and middle grades.

sentences.zh: 既經諭令各省仿辦，應酌照將來選舉章程，用資鼓勵。

sentences.zh: 辛丑，兩宮迴鑾。

translations.literal: In Xinchou, the two courts returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1901 the court returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 以創痛鉅深，力求改革。

translations.literal: Grieving deeply over fresh wounds, they strove earnestly for reform.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply wounded, they pressed urgently for reform.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諭曰：「興學育才，實為當今急務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict stated: "Promoting learning and cultivating talent are truly urgent tasks of the present day.
translations.idiomatic: In December an edict declared: "Promoting education and cultivating talent are urgent national tasks.

sentences.zh: 京師首善之區，尤宜加意作育，以樹風聲。

translations.literal: The capital, foremost region of excellence, should especially receive nurturing care to set the tone for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The capital, as the nation's model, must especially nurture talent to set an example.

sentences.zh: 前建大學，應切實舉辦。

translations.literal: The university previously established should be earnestly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The university previously planned must be earnestly established.

sentences.zh: 派張百熙為管學大臣，責成經理，務期端正趨鄉，造就通才。

translations.literal: Zhang Baixi was appointed superintendent of studies and charged with management, with the duty to set a correct direction and train versatile talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baixi was appointed superintendent and charged to manage affairs, set a proper course, and train versatile talent.

sentences.zh: 其裁定章程，妥議具奏。

translations.idiomatic: He was to draft regulations and memorialize.

sentences.zh: 」旋諭將同文館併入大學堂，毋庸隸外務部。

translations.idiomatic: An edict soon merged the Tongwen Guan into the university, removing it from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，百熙奏籌辦大學堂情形豫定辦法一條，言：「各國學制，幼童於蒙學卒業後入小學，三年卒業升中學，又三年升高等學，又三年升大學。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year, Baixi memorialized on planning the university and preset one method, stating: "Every country's school system: after children graduate from elementary schooling they enter primary school, graduate in three years and rise to middle school, three more years to higher school, three more years to university.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1902 Zhang Baixi memorialized on the university and proposed: "In every country, after elementary schooling children enter primary school for three years, then middle school for three, higher school for three, then university.

sentences.zh: 以中國准之，小學即縣學堂，中學即府學堂，高等學即省學堂。

translations.literal: Compared with China, primary school is the county school, middle school the prefectural school, higher school the provincial school.
translations.idiomatic: In Chinese terms, primary school is the county school, middle the prefectural, higher the provincial.

sentences.zh: 目前無應入大學肄業之學生，通融辦法，惟有暫時不設專門，先設立一高等學為大學豫備科。

translations.literal: At present there are no students ready to enter the university; a flexible method is that for the time being no specialized departments be set up, but first a higher school be established as the university preparatory course.
translations.idiomatic: No students were yet ready for university; the interim plan was to establish a higher school as the university preparatory division without specialized departments.

sentences.zh: 分政、藝二科，以經史、政治、法律、通商、理財等事隸政科，以聲、光、電、化、農、工、醫、算等事隸藝科。

translations.literal: It was divided into civil and technical branches: classics, history, politics, law, commerce, and finance under the civil branch; sound, light, electricity, chemistry, agriculture, engineering, medicine, and mathematics under the technical branch.
translations.idiomatic: It was divided into civil and technical tracks: the civil track covered classics, history, politics, law, commerce, and finance; the technical track covered physics, chemistry, agriculture, engineering, medicine, and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 查京外學堂，辦有成效者，以湖北自強學堂、上海南洋公學為最。

translations.literal: Examining schools inside and outside the capital that had achieved results, the Hubei Self-Strengthening Academy and Shanghai Nanyang Public School ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Among effective schools, the Hubei Self-Strengthening Academy and Shanghai Nanyang Public School ranked highest.

sentences.zh: 此外如京師同文館，上海廣方言館，廣東時敏、浙江求是等學堂，開辦皆在數年以上，不乏合格之才。

translations.literal: Besides these, the capital Tongwen Guan, Shanghai Guangfangyan Guan, Guangdong Shimin, Zhejiang Qiushi, and other schools, all operating for many years, had no lack of qualified talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Beijing Tongwen Guan, Shanghai Guangfangyan Guan, Guangdong Shimin, Zhejiang Qiushi, and others, open for years, also supplied qualified students.

sentences.zh: 更由各省督、撫、學政考取府、州、縣高材生，咨送來京，覆試如格，入堂肄業。

translations.literal: Further, governors-general, governors, and education commissioners in each province were to examine and send talented students from prefectures, departments, and counties to the capital; upon passing re-examination they would enter to study.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial authorities were also to examine and send talented local students to the capital; those who passed re-examination would enroll.

sentences.zh: 三年卒業，及格者升大學正科。

translations.literal: After three years of graduation, those who passed advanced to the university proper.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, those who passed advanced to the university proper.

sentences.zh: 不及格者，分別留學、撤退。

translations.literal: Those who failed were respectively retained for further study or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Failures were retained for further study or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 大學豫科與各省省學堂卒業生程度相同，由管學大臣考驗合格，請旨賞給舉人。

translations.literal: The university preparatory course matched the level of provincial school graduates; the superintendent, upon passing examination, would memorialize for conferral of juren rank.
translations.idiomatic: Preparatory graduates matched provincial school level; the superintendent, after examination, would memorialize for juren rank.

sentences.zh: 正科卒業，考驗合格，請旨賞給進士。

translations.literal: Upon graduation from the proper course and passing examination, memorialization was made for conferral of jinshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: Proper-course graduates who passed would receive jinshi rank by memorial.

sentences.zh: 惟國家需材孔亟，欲收急效而少棄才，則有速成教員一法。

translations.literal: Only because the state urgently needed talent and wished quick results without wasting ability, there was the method of accelerated teacher training.
translations.idiomatic: Because the state urgently needed talent and sought quick results without wasting ability, an accelerated teacher-training track was added.

sentences.zh: 於預備科外設速成科，分二門：曰仕學館，曰師範館。

translations.literal: Besides the preparatory course, an accelerated course was established with two divisions: the Official Studies Hall and the Normal Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the preparatory division, an accelerated course offered two halls: Official Studies and Normal.

sentences.zh: 凡京員五品以下、八品以上，外官道員以下、教職以上，皆許考入仕學館。

translations.literal: Capital officials from fifth rank down to eighth rank up, and provincial officials from circuit intendant down and educational officials up, might all enter the Official Studies Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials from fifth rank down to eighth rank up, and provincial officials from circuit intendant down and educational officials up, might enroll in the Official Studies Hall.

sentences.zh: 舉、貢、生、監，皆許考入師範館。

translations.literal: Juren, gongsheng, students, and supervised students might all enter the Normal Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Juren, gongsheng, students, and supervised students might enroll in the Normal Hall.

sentences.zh: 仕學三年卒業，擇尤保獎。

translations.literal: Official Studies graduates after three years; the outstanding received preferential recommendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Official Studies graduates after three years; the best received preferential recommendation.

sentences.zh: 師範三年卒業，擇優異者帶領引見。

translations.literal: Normal graduates after three years; the especially outstanding were led in audience before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Normal graduates after three years; the outstanding were presented at court.

sentences.zh: 生准作貢生，貢生准作舉人，舉人准作進士，分別給予准作小學、中學教員文憑。

translations.literal: Students were granted quasi-gongsheng status, gongsheng quasi-juren, juren quasi-jinshi, with credentials respectively authorizing them as primary or middle school teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Students received quasi-gongsheng status, gongsheng quasi-juren, juren quasi-jinshi, with credentials authorizing them as primary or middle school teachers.

sentences.zh: 蓋豫科生必齲年歲最富、學術稍精者，再加練習，儲為真正合格之才。

translations.literal: This was because preparatory students had to be those richest in years and of somewhat refined learning; with further practice they would be stored up as truly qualified talent.
translations.idiomatic: Preparatory students had to be the youngest and best prepared, to be trained into fully qualified talent.

sentences.zh: 速成生則取更事較多、立志猛進者，取其聽從速化之效。

translations.literal: Accelerated students took those with more experience and fierce determination, seeking the effect of rapid transformation through obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Accelerated students were older, more experienced men seeking rapid transformation.

sentences.zh: 至增建校舍，附設譯局，廣購書籍、儀器，尤以寬籌經費為根原。

translations.literal: As for expanding buildings, attaching a translation bureau, and widely purchasing books and instruments, securing ample funds was especially the root.
translations.idiomatic: Expanding buildings, adding a translation bureau, and purchasing books and apparatus all depended above all on ample funding.

sentences.zh: 經費分兩項：一，華俄道勝銀行存款之息金，全數撥歸大學堂；

translations.literal: Funds were divided into two items: first, interest on deposits at the Russo-Chinese Bank was entirely allocated to the university;
translations.idiomatic: Funding came from two sources: interest on Russo-Chinese Bank deposits went entirely to the university;

sentences.zh: 一，請飭各省籌助經費，每年大省二萬金，中省一萬金，小省五千金，常年撥解京師。

translations.literal: second, provinces were ordered to contribute annual subsidies—twenty thousand taels for large provinces, ten thousand for medium, five thousand for small—remitted regularly to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: provinces were to contribute annual subsidies—twenty thousand taels for large provinces, ten thousand for medium, five thousand for small.

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Baixi, following the draft school regulations, memorialized: "China and abroad, past and present, learning differs, yet the purpose of practical use is one.
translations.idiomatic: In July Zhang Baixi, following his draft regulations, memorialized: "Learning differs across ages and nations, yet practical purpose is one.

sentences.zh: 歐、美、日本諸邦現行制度，頗與中國古昔盛時良法相同。

translations.literal: Present systems in Europe, America, and Japan resemble good methods of China's ancient flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: Present systems in Europe, America, and Japan resemble China's ancient flourishing institutions.

sentences.zh: 禮記載家有塾，黨有庠，州有序，國有學。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites records that families had tutors, districts had village schools, states had academies, and the realm had the imperial college.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites records family tutors, district schools, state academies, and the imperial college.

sentences.zh: 比之各國，則國學即大學，家塾、黨庠、州序即蒙學、小學、中學。

translations.literal: Compared with various countries, the imperial college is the university, and family tutors, village schools, and state academies are elementary, primary, and middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial college corresponds to the university; family, district, and state schools to elementary, primary, and middle schools.

sentences.zh: 等級蓋甚分明。

translations.literal: The grades are very clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The grades were clearly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 周以前選舉、學校合而為一，漢以後專重選舉，及隋設進士科以來，士皆殫精神於詩、賦、策、論，所謂學校，名存而巳。

translations.literal: Before the Zhou, selection and schools were united; after Han selection alone was emphasized; since the Sui established the jinshi degree, gentlemen poured their spirit into poetry, fu, policy essays, and discourse—so-called schools existed in name only.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Zhou, selection and schooling were one; after Han, selection dominated; since the Sui jinshi degree, scholars poured effort into examination essays—schools existed in name only.

sentences.zh: 今日而議振興教育，必以真能復學校之舊為第一要圖。

translations.literal: To discuss reviving education today, truly restoring the old schools must be the first essential.
translations.idiomatic: To revive education today, truly restoring schools must be the first task.

sentences.zh: 雖中外政教風氣原本不同，然其條目秩序之至賾而不可亂，不必盡泥其跡，不能不兼取其長。

translations.literal: Though Chinese and foreign government, teaching, and customs differ in origin, yet in orderly arrangement of items and sequence the principles are so intricate they cannot be disordered; one need not follow every trace, yet cannot fail to take the best of each.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chinese and foreign institutions differ, their orderly structure cannot be ignored; one need not copy every detail yet must take the best of each.

sentences.zh: 謹上溯古制，參考列邦，擬定京師大學暨各省高等學、中學、小學、蒙學章程，候欽定頒行各省，核實興辦。

translations.literal: Reverently tracing ancient institutions, consulting foreign states, he drafted regulations for the Imperial University and provincial higher, middle, primary, and elementary schools, awaiting imperial confirmation for issuance to the provinces for earnest establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing ancient institutions and consulting foreign models, he drafted regulations for the Imperial University and provincial higher, middle, primary, and elementary schools for imperial approval and provincial implementation.

sentences.zh: 凡名是實非之學堂及庸濫充數之教習，一律從嚴整頓。

translations.literal: All schools false in name and true in nothing, and instructors who filled posts without qualification, were to be strictly rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Schools that were nominal only and unqualified teachers were to be strictly rectified.

sentences.zh: 」詔下各省督撫，按照規條實力奉行。

translations.literal: " An edict was sent to provincial governors to earnestly enforce the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered provincial governors to enforce the regulations earnestly.

sentences.zh: 是為欽定學堂章程。

translations.literal: This was the imperially approved school regulations.
translations.idiomatic: These were the imperially approved school regulations.

sentences.zh: 教育之有系統自此始。

translations.literal: Systematic organization of education began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Systematic education began here.

sentences.zh: 京師大學堂分大學院、大學專門分科、大學豫備科。

translations.literal: The Imperial University was divided into the university faculty, specialized university departments, and the university preparatory course.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University comprised a research faculty, specialized departments, and a preparatory course.

sentences.zh: 附設者，仕學、師範兩館。

translations.literal: Attached were the Official Studies and Normal halls.
translations.idiomatic: Attached were the Official Studies and Normal halls.

sentences.zh: 大學院主研究，不講授，不立課程。

translations.literal: The university faculty was devoted to research, not lecturing, and had no fixed curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: The university faculty conducted research without lecturing or fixed curriculum.

sentences.zh: 專門分科凡七：曰政治科，曰文學科，曰格致科，曰農業科，曰工藝科，曰商務科，曰醫術科。

translations.literal: Specialized departments numbered seven: political science, literature, natural science, agriculture, engineering, commerce, and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Specialized departments numbered seven: political science, literature, natural science, agriculture, engineering, commerce, and medicine.

sentences.zh: 政治科分目二：政治，法律。

translations.literal: The political science department was divided into two subjects: politics and law.
translations.idiomatic: The political science department comprised politics and law.

sentences.zh: 文學科分目七：經學，史學，理學，諸子，掌故，詞章，外國語言文字。

translations.literal: The literature department was divided into seven subjects: classics, history, Neo-Confucian philosophy, masters, institutional precedents, literary composition, and foreign languages and script.
translations.idiomatic: The literature department comprised seven subjects: classics, history, Neo-Confucian philosophy, masters, institutional precedents, literary composition, and foreign languages and script.

sentences.zh: 格致科分目六：天文，地質，高等算學，化學，物理，動植物。

translations.literal: The natural science department was divided into six subjects: astronomy, geology, advanced mathematics, chemistry, physics, and zoology and botany.
translations.idiomatic: The natural science department comprised six subjects: astronomy, geology, advanced mathematics, chemistry, physics, and zoology and botany.

sentences.zh: 農業科分目四：農藝，農業化學，林學，獸醫。

translations.literal: The agriculture department was divided into four subjects: agronomy, agricultural chemistry, forestry, and veterinary medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The agriculture department comprised four subjects: agronomy, agricultural chemistry, forestry, and veterinary medicine.

sentences.zh: 工藝科分目八：土木，機器，造船，造兵器，電氣，建築，應用化學，採礦冶金。

translations.literal: The engineering department was divided into eight subjects: civil engineering, machinery, shipbuilding, arms manufacture, electrical engineering, architecture, applied chemistry, and mining and metallurgy.
translations.idiomatic: The engineering department comprised eight subjects: civil engineering, machinery, shipbuilding, arms manufacture, electrical engineering, architecture, applied chemistry, and mining and metallurgy.

sentences.zh: 商務科分目六：簿記，產業製造，商業語言，商法，商業史，商業地理。

translations.literal: The commerce department was divided into six subjects: bookkeeping, industrial production, commercial languages, commercial law, commercial history, and commercial geography.
translations.idiomatic: The commerce department comprised six subjects: bookkeeping, industrial production, commercial languages, commercial law, commercial history, and commercial geography.

sentences.zh: 醫術科分目二：醫學，藥學。

translations.literal: The medicine department was divided into two subjects: medicine and pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: The medicine department comprised medicine and pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 豫備科分政、藝兩科。

translations.literal: The preparatory course was divided into political and technical streams.
translations.idiomatic: The preparatory course was split into political and technical streams.

sentences.zh: 政科課目：倫理，經學，諸子，詞章，算學，中外史，中外輿地，外國文，物理，名學，法學，理財，體操。

translations.literal: Political stream courses: ethics, classics, masters, literary composition, mathematics, Chinese and foreign history, Chinese and foreign geography, foreign languages, physics, logic, law, finance, and physical education.
translations.idiomatic: The political stream covered ethics, classics, masters, literary composition, mathematics, Chinese and foreign history and geography, foreign languages, physics, logic, law, finance, and physical education.

sentences.zh: 藝科課目：倫理，中外史，外國文，算學，物理，化學，動植物，地質及礦產，圖畫，體操。

translations.literal: Technical stream courses: ethics, Chinese and foreign history, foreign languages, mathematics, physics, chemistry, zoology and botany, geology and mineral resources, drawing, and physical education.
translations.idiomatic: The technical stream covered ethics, Chinese and foreign history, foreign languages, mathematics, physics, chemistry, zoology and botany, geology and mineral resources, drawing, and physical education.

sentences.zh: 為入專理某科便利計，得增減若干科目。

translations.literal: For convenience in entering a specialized department, certain subjects might be added or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects could be added or reduced as convenient for specializing in a particular department.

sentences.zh: 各三年卒業。

translations.literal: Each required three years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Each required three years to complete.

sentences.zh: 仕學館課目：算學，博物，物理，外國文，輿地，史學，掌故，理財，交涉，法律，政治。

translations.literal: Official Studies Hall courses: mathematics, natural history, physics, foreign languages, geography, history, institutional precedents, finance, diplomacy, law, and politics.
translations.idiomatic: The Official Studies Hall taught mathematics, natural history, physics, foreign languages, geography, history, institutional precedents, finance, diplomacy, law, and politics.

sentences.zh: 師範館課目：倫理，經學，教育，習字，作文，算學，中外史，中外輿地，博物，物理，化學，外國文，圖畫，體操。

translations.literal: Normal Hall courses: ethics, classics, education, penmanship, composition, mathematics, Chinese and foreign history, Chinese and foreign geography, natural history, physics, chemistry, foreign languages, drawing, and physical education.
translations.idiomatic: The Normal Hall taught ethics, classics, education, penmanship, composition, mathematics, Chinese and foreign history and geography, natural history, physics, chemistry, foreign languages, drawing, and physical education.

sentences.zh: 各省高等學堂為中學卒業之升途，又為入分科大學之豫備。

translations.literal: Provincial higher schools were the path upward for middle school graduates and also served as preparation for entering the university's specialized departments.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial higher schools were the next step for middle school graduates and prepared students for the university's specialized departments.

sentences.zh: 分政、藝兩科。

translations.literal: They were divided into political and technical streams.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into political and technical streams.

sentences.zh: 課程與大學豫科同。

translations.literal: The curriculum was the same as that of the university preparatory course.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum matched that of the university preparatory course.

sentences.zh: 三年卒業。

translations.literal: Three years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Three years to complete.

sentences.zh: 高等學外，得附設農、工、商、醫高等實業學堂，亦中學卒業生升入。

translations.literal: Besides higher schools, agricultural, industrial, commercial, and medical higher vocational schools might be attached; middle school graduates also entered these.
translations.idiomatic: Higher schools might also have attached agricultural, industrial, commercial, and medical vocational schools, which middle school graduates entered as well.

sentences.zh: 教授用專科教員制，各任一門。

translations.literal: Instruction employed a specialist-teacher system, each teacher responsible for one subject.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction used specialist teachers, each responsible for one subject.

sentences.zh: 中學堂，為高等小學卒業之升途，即為入高等學之豫備。

translations.literal: Middle schools were the path upward for higher primary graduates and served as preparation for higher schools.
translations.idiomatic: Middle schools were the next step for higher primary graduates and prepared students for higher schools.

sentences.zh: 課目：修身，讀經，算學，詞章，中外史，中外輿地，外國文，圖畫，博物，物理，化學，體操。

translations.literal: Courses: moral cultivation, scripture reading, mathematics, literary composition, Chinese and foreign history, Chinese and foreign geography, foreign languages, drawing, natural history, physics, chemistry, and physical education.
translations.idiomatic: Courses included moral cultivation, scripture reading, mathematics, literary composition, Chinese and foreign history and geography, foreign languages, drawing, natural history, physics, chemistry, and physical education.

sentences.zh: 四年卒業。

translations.literal: Four years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Four years to complete.

sentences.zh: 中學外，得設中等農、工、商實業學堂，高小卒業生不原治普通學者入之。

translations.literal: Besides middle schools, intermediate agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools might be established; higher primary graduates who did not wish to pursue general studies entered these.
translations.idiomatic: Intermediate agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools might also be established for higher primary graduates who did not wish to pursue general studies.

sentences.zh: 又附設師範學堂，課目視中學，惟酌減外國文，加教育學、教授法。

translations.literal: Attached normal schools might also be set up; their courses followed the middle school pattern, except that foreign languages were somewhat reduced and pedagogy and teaching methods were added.
translations.idiomatic: Attached normal schools might follow the middle school curriculum, with foreign languages somewhat reduced and pedagogy and teaching methods added.

sentences.zh: 得合兩班或三班，以兩三教員各任數科目，分教之。

translations.literal: Two or three classes might be combined, with two or three teachers each taking several subjects and teaching in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three classes might be combined, with two or three teachers each covering several subjects in rotation.

sentences.zh: 小學堂分高等、尋常二級。

translations.literal: Primary schools were divided into higher and ordinary levels.
translations.idiomatic: Primary schools were divided into higher and ordinary levels.

sentences.zh: 兒童自六歲起，受蒙學四年。

translations.literal: Children from age six received four years of elementary instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Children from age six received four years of elementary instruction.

sentences.zh: 十歲入尋常小學，修業三年。

translations.literal: At ten they entered ordinary primary school for three years.
translations.idiomatic: At ten they entered ordinary primary school for three years.

sentences.zh: 此七年定為義務教育。

translations.literal: These seven years were designated compulsory education.
translations.idiomatic: These seven years were designated compulsory education.

sentences.zh: 十三歲入高等小學，三年卒業。

translations.literal: At thirteen they entered higher primary school, completing in three years.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen they entered higher primary school, completing in three years.

sentences.zh: 得附設簡易農、工、商實業學堂，尋常小學卒業者入之。

translations.literal: Simple agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools might be attached; ordinary primary graduates entered these.
translations.idiomatic: Simple agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools might be attached for ordinary primary graduates.

sentences.zh: 尋常小學課目：修身、讀經、作文、習字、史學、輿地、算術、體操。

translations.literal: Ordinary primary courses: moral cultivation, scripture reading, composition, penmanship, history, geography, arithmetic, and physical education.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary primary courses included moral cultivation, scripture reading, composition, penmanship, history, geography, arithmetic, and physical education.

sentences.zh: 高等小學課目，增讀古文辭、理科、圖畫，餘同尋常小學。

translations.literal: Higher primary courses added classical prose, natural science, and drawing; the rest were the same as ordinary primary.
translations.idiomatic: Higher primary courses added classical prose, natural science, and drawing; the rest matched ordinary primary.

sentences.zh: 教授採用級任制。

translations.literal: Instruction adopted the homeroom-teacher system.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction adopted the homeroom-teacher system.

sentences.zh: 正教習外，得置副教習。

translations.literal: Besides the head teacher, assistant teachers might be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the head teacher, assistant teachers might be appointed.

sentences.zh: 蒙學堂屬義務教育，府、廳、州、縣、城、鎮、鄉、集均應設立。

translations.literal: Elementary schools fell within compulsory education and were to be established in every prefecture, department, subprefecture, county, city, market town, village, and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary schools were part of compulsory education and were to be established in every prefecture, department, subprefecture, county, city, market town, village, and hamlet.

sentences.zh: 凡義塾或家塾，應照蒙學課程，核實改辦。

translations.literal: All charity schools and private tutors' schools were to be verified and reformed according to the elementary curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: All charity schools and private tutors' schools were to be verified and reformed according to the elementary curriculum.

sentences.zh: 課目同尋常小學，惟作文易以字課。

translations.literal: The courses were the same as ordinary primary, except that composition was replaced by character drills.
translations.idiomatic: The courses matched ordinary primary, except that composition was replaced by character drills.

sentences.zh: 蒙學宗旨，在於改良私塾，故章程規定，頗注重教授法之改善，於兒童身心之體察，三致意焉。

translations.literal: The aim of elementary schools was to reform private tutoring schools; the regulations therefore placed considerable emphasis on improving teaching methods and repeatedly addressed the care of children's minds and bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary schools aimed to reform private tutoring schools; the regulations therefore emphasized improved teaching methods and repeatedly addressed the care of children's minds and bodies.

sentences.zh: 至學生出身獎勵，小學卒業，獎給附生；

translations.literal: As for student honors and rewards: upon completing primary school, one was granted the rank of government licentiate;
translations.idiomatic: As for student honors and rewards: upon completing primary school, one was granted the rank of government licentiate;

sentences.zh: 中學卒業，獎給貢生；

translations.literal: upon completing middle school, one was granted the rank of tribute student;
