translations.idiomatic: upon completing middle school, one was granted the rank of tribute student;

sentences.zh: 高等學卒業，獎給舉人；

translations.literal: upon completing higher school, one was granted the rank of provincial graduate;
translations.idiomatic: upon completing higher school, one was granted the rank of provincial graduate;

sentences.zh: 大學分科卒業，獎給進士。

translations.literal: upon completing a university specialized department, one was granted the rank of presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: upon completing a university specialized department, one was granted the rank of presented scholar.

sentences.zh: 各省師範卒業，照大學師範館例給獎。

translations.literal: Graduates of provincial normal schools received awards according to the precedent of the Imperial Normal Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial normal school graduates received awards according to the precedent of the Imperial Normal Hall.

sentences.zh: 其大較也。

translations.literal: Such was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general outline.

sentences.zh: 欽定章程雖未臻完備，然已有系統之組織。

translations.literal: Although the imperially authorized regulations were not yet fully complete, they already possessed a systematic organization.
translations.idiomatic: Although the imperially authorized regulations were not yet fully complete, they already formed a systematic organization.

sentences.zh: 頒布未及二年，旋又廢止。

translations.literal: Less than two years after promulgation, they were abruptly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Less than two years after promulgation, they were abruptly abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是百熙招致海內名流，任大學堂各職。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Baixi had invited celebrated figures from throughout the realm to fill the various posts of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Baixi had invited celebrated figures from throughout the realm to fill the Imperial University's various posts.

sentences.zh: 吳汝綸為總教習，赴日本參觀學校。

translations.literal: Wu Rulun served as chief instructor and went to Japan to inspect schools.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rulun served as chief instructor and went to Japan to inspect schools.

sentences.zh: 適留日學生迭起風潮，諑謠繁興，黨爭日甚。

translations.literal: Just then Chinese students in Japan repeatedly stirred up disturbances; slander and rumor proliferated, and factional strife grew daily fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Chinese students in Japan repeatedly stirred up disturbances; slander and rumor proliferated, and factional strife grew fiercer by the day.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月，命榮慶會同百熙管理大學堂事宜。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year, Rongqing was ordered to join Zhang Baixi in administering the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year [1903], Rongqing was ordered to join Zhang Baixi in administering the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 二人學術思想，既各不同，用人行政，意見尤多歧異。

translations.literal: The two men's scholarly outlooks already differed; in appointments and administration their views diverged still more sharply.
translations.idiomatic: The two men's scholarly outlooks already differed; in appointments and administration their views diverged still more sharply.

sentences.zh: 時鄂督張之洞入覲。

translations.literal: At that time Huguang Governor-General Zhang Zhidong came to the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huguang Governor-General Zhang Zhidong came to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 之洞負海內重望，於川、晉、粵、鄂，曾創設書院及學堂。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great prestige throughout the realm; in Sichuan, Shanxi, Guangdong, and Hubei he had founded academies and schools.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great prestige throughout the realm; in Sichuan, Shanxi, Guangdong, and Hubei he had founded academies and schools.

sentences.zh: 著勸學篇，傳誦一時；

translations.literal: He authored Exhortation to Learning, which was widely circulated for a time;
translations.idiomatic: He authored Exhortation to Learning, which was widely circulated for a time;

sentences.zh: 尤抱整飭學務之素志。

translations.literal: and had long cherished a resolve to reform educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and had long cherished a resolve to reform educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，榮慶約同百熙奏請添派之洞會商學務，詔飭之洞會同管學大臣釐定一切學堂章程，期推行無弊。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month, Rongqing jointly with Zhang Baixi memorialized requesting that Zhang Zhidong be additionally assigned to consult on educational affairs; an edict ordered Zhang Zhidong to join the Minister of Education in settling all school regulations, so that implementation might be free of abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month, Rongqing and Zhang Baixi jointly memorialized requesting that Zhang Zhidong be additionally assigned to consult on educational affairs; an edict ordered Zhang Zhidong to join the Minister of Education in settling all school regulations so that implementation might be free of abuses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，百熙、榮慶、之洞會奏重訂學堂章程，言：「各省初辦學堂，難得深通教育理法之人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zhang Baixi, Rongqing, and Zhang Zhidong jointly memorialized on the revised school regulations, stating: "When provinces first establish schools, it is hard to find persons thoroughly versed in educational theory and method.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Zhang Baixi, Rongqing, and Zhang Zhidong jointly memorialized on the revised school regulations, stating: "When provinces first establish schools, it is hard to find persons thoroughly versed in educational theory and method.

sentences.zh: 學生率取諸原業科舉之士，未經小學陶鎔而來，言論行為，不免軼於範圍之外。

translations.literal: Students were mostly drawn from those who had formerly pursued the civil service examinations; without the shaping of primary schooling, their speech and conduct unavoidably fell outside proper bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Students were mostly drawn from those who had formerly pursued the civil service examinations; without the shaping of primary schooling, their speech and conduct unavoidably fell outside proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 此次奉諭會商釐定，詳細推求，倍加審慎。

translations.literal: This time, obeying the imperial command to consult and settle the matter, we examined it closely and proceeded with redoubled caution.
translations.idiomatic: This time, obeying the imperial command to consult and settle the matter, we examined it closely and proceeded with redoubled caution.

sentences.zh: 博考外國各項學堂課程門目，參酌變通，擇其宜者用之，其於中國不相宜者缺之，科目名稱不可解者改之，過涉繁重者減之。

translations.literal: We broadly examined the courses and subjects of foreign schools of every kind, adapting and modifying them as we saw fit; what suited China we adopted, what did not suit China we omitted, incomprehensible subject titles we changed, and what was excessively burdensome we reduced.
translations.idiomatic: We broadly examined the courses and subjects of foreign schools of every kind, adapting them as we saw fit: what suited China we adopted, what did not we omitted, incomprehensible titles we changed, and what was excessively burdensome we reduced.

sentences.zh: 無論何等學堂，均以忠孝為本，以中國經史之學為基，俾學生心術壹歸於純正。

translations.literal: Whatever the school, loyalty and filial piety were to be the foundation and Chinese classics and history the base, so that students' minds might uniformly return to purity and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the school, loyalty and filial piety were to be the foundation and Chinese classics and history the base, so that students' minds might uniformly return to purity and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 而後以西學瀹其智識，練其藝能，務期他日成材，各適實用。

translations.literal: Only then would Western learning enrich their intelligence and train their skills, with the aim that in time they would become productive talents, each suited to practical employment.
translations.idiomatic: Only then would Western learning enrich their intelligence and train their skills, with the aim that in time they would become productive talents, each suited to practical employment.

sentences.zh: 擬成初等小學、高等小學、中學、高等學各章程，大學附通儒院章程。

translations.literal: Regulations were drafted for elementary primary schools, higher primary schools, middle schools, and higher schools, together with regulations for the university and the attached College of Universal Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were drafted for elementary primary schools, higher primary schools, middle schools, and higher schools, together with regulations for the university and the attached College of Universal Learning.

sentences.zh: 原章有蒙學名目，所列實即外國初等小學之事。

translations.literal: The original regulations had a term "elementary learning," but what they listed was in fact what foreign countries called elementary primary schooling.
translations.idiomatic: The original regulations used the term "elementary learning," but what they listed was in fact what foreign countries called elementary primary schooling.

sentences.zh: 外國蒙養院，一名稚園，參酌其意，訂為蒙養院章程及家庭教育法。

translations.literal: Foreign countries had nursery schools, also called kindergartens; considering their intent, regulations for nursery schools and family education were drafted.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign countries had nursery schools, also called kindergartens; considering their intent, regulations for nursery schools and family education were drafted.

sentences.zh: 此原章所有，而增補其缺略者也。

translations.literal: These were items already in the original regulations, now supplemented where they had been incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: These were items already in the original regulations, now supplemented where they had been incomplete.

sentences.zh: 辦理學堂，首重師範。

translations.literal: In running schools, teacher training came first.
translations.idiomatic: In running schools, teacher training came first.

sentences.zh: 原訂師範館章程，系僅就京城情形試辦，尚屬簡略。

translations.literal: The originally drawn regulations for the Normal Hall were merely a trial arrangement suited to the capital and remained quite bare.
translations.idiomatic: The originally drawn regulations for the Normal Hall were merely a trial arrangement suited to the capital and remained quite bare.

sentences.zh: 另擬初級、優級師範學堂章程，並任用教員章程，京城師範館改照優級師範辦理。

translations.literal: Separate regulations were drafted for elementary and advanced normal schools, along with regulations for the appointment of teachers; the capital Normal Hall was converted to operate as an advanced normal school.
translations.idiomatic: Separate regulations were drafted for elementary and advanced normal schools, along with regulations for the appointment of teachers; the capital Normal Hall was converted to operate as an advanced normal school.

sentences.zh: 此外仕學館屬暫設，不在各學堂統系之內，原章應暫仍舊。

translations.literal: Beyond this, the Official Studies Hall was temporary and lay outside the school system; the original regulations were temporarily left unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, the Official Studies Hall was temporary and lay outside the school system; the original regulations were temporarily left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 譯學館即方言學堂；

translations.literal: The Translation College was the School of Dialects;
translations.idiomatic: The Translation College was the School of Dialects;

sentences.zh: 進士館系奉特旨，令新進士概入學堂肄業，課程與各學堂不同，並酌定章程課目。

translations.literal: the Presented Scholars College was established by special edict requiring all newly minted jinshi to enter for study; its curriculum differed from other schools, and regulations and courses were likewise drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: the Presented Scholars College was established by special edict requiring all newly minted jinshi to enter for study; its curriculum differed from other schools, and regulations and courses were likewise drawn up.

sentences.zh: 又國民生計，莫要於農、工、商實業，興辦實業學堂，有百益而無一弊，另擬初等、中等、高等農、工、商實業學堂章程，附實業補習普通學堂、藝徒學堂、實業教員講習所各章程。

translations.literal: Moreover, nothing mattered more for the people's livelihood than agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocations; establishing vocational schools yielded a hundred benefits without a single harm. Separate regulations were drafted for elementary, intermediate, and higher agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools, together with regulations for vocational supplementary general schools, apprentice schools, and vocational teacher training institutes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, nothing mattered more for the people's livelihood than agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocations; establishing vocational schools yielded a hundred benefits without a single harm. Separate regulations were drafted for elementary, intermediate, and higher agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools, together with regulations for vocational supplementary general schools, apprentice schools, and vocational teacher training institutes.

sentences.zh: 此原章未及，而別加編訂者也。

translations.literal: These were matters the original regulations had not reached, now separately compiled and added.
translations.idiomatic: These were matters the original regulations had not reached, now separately compiled and added.

sentences.zh: 又中國禮教政俗與各國不同，少年初學，胸無定識，哤雜浮囂，在所不免。

translations.literal: Moreover, China's rites, teaching, politics, and customs differed from those of other countries; youths just beginning to study, with no settled judgment, inevitably fell into confused clamor and strident behavior.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, China's rites, teaching, politics, and customs differed from those of other countries; youths just beginning to study, with no settled judgment, inevitably fell into confused clamor and strident behavior.

sentences.zh: 規範不容不肅，稽察不容不嚴。

translations.literal: Standards could not but be strict, and oversight could not but be rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Standards could not but be strict, and oversight could not but be rigorous.

sentences.zh: 特訂立規條，申明禁令，為學堂管理通則。

translations.literal: Special rules were established and prohibitions clearly set forth as general regulations for school administration.
translations.idiomatic: Special rules were established and prohibitions clearly set forth as general regulations for school administration.

sentences.zh: 並將設學宗旨、立法要義，總括髮明，為學務綱要。

translations.literal: The purposes of establishing schools and the essential principles of legislation were likewise summarized and set forth as the general outline of educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The purposes of establishing schools and the essential principles of legislation were likewise summarized and expounded as the general outline of educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 果能按照現定章程認真舉辦，民智可開，國力可富，人才可成，不致別生流弊。

translations.literal: If the presently settled regulations were earnestly carried out, popular intelligence could be awakened, national strength enriched, talent formed, and no further abuses allowed to arise.
translations.idiomatic: If the presently settled regulations were earnestly carried out, popular intelligence could be awakened, national strength enriched, talent formed, and no further abuses allowed to arise.

sentences.zh: 至學生畢業考試，升級、入學考試及獎勵錄用之法，亦經詳定專章，伏候裁定。

translations.literal: As for graduation examinations, promotion and entrance examinations, and methods of reward and employment, separate chapters had also been carefully drafted, pending imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: As for graduation examinations, promotion and entrance examinations, and methods of reward and employment, separate chapters had also been carefully drafted, pending imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「奉旨興辦學堂，兩年有餘。

translations.literal: They further memorialized: "By imperial command schools were established; more than two years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: They further memorialized: "By imperial command schools were established; more than two years have passed.

sentences.zh: 至今各省未能多設者，經費難籌也。

translations.literal: Yet the reason provinces have still been unable to establish many is that funds are hard to raise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the reason provinces have still been unable to establish many is that funds are hard to raise.

sentences.zh: 經費所以不能捐集者，科舉未停，天下士林謂朝廷之意並未專重學堂也。

translations.literal: The reason funds could not be collected through donation was that the civil service examinations had not been suspended; scholars throughout the realm believed the court's intent did not yet specially favor schools.
translations.idiomatic: The reason funds could not be collected through donation was that the civil service examinations had not been suspended; scholars throughout the realm believed the court's intent did not yet specially favor schools.

sentences.zh: 科舉不變通裁減，人情不免觀望，紳富孰肯籌捐？

translations.literal: Unless the examinations were reformed and reduced, people would inevitably wait and see—what gentry or wealthy men would be willing to contribute?
translations.idiomatic: Unless the examinations were reformed and reduced, people would inevitably wait and see—what gentry or wealthy men would be willing to contribute?

sentences.zh: 經費斷不能籌，學堂斷不能多。

translations.literal: Funds absolutely could not be raised, and schools absolutely could not be multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Funds absolutely could not be raised, and schools absolutely could not be multiplied.

sentences.zh: 入學堂者，恃有科舉一途為退步，不肯專心鄉學，且不肯恪守學規。

translations.literal: Those who entered schools relied on the civil service examinations as a fallback and were unwilling to devote themselves wholeheartedly to study, nor willing to observe school regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who entered schools relied on the civil service examinations as a fallback and were unwilling to devote themselves wholeheartedly to study, nor willing to observe school regulations.

sentences.zh: 況科舉文字多剽竊，學堂功課務實修；

translations.literal: Moreover, examination essays were often plagiarized, whereas school work required solid attainment;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, examination essays were often plagiarized, whereas school work required solid attainment;

sentences.zh: 科舉止憑一日之短長，學堂必盡累年之研究；

translations.literal: the examinations judged by a single day's performance, whereas schools required years of sustained research;
translations.idiomatic: the examinations judged by a single day's performance, whereas schools required years of sustained research;

sentences.zh: 科舉但取詞章，學堂並重行檢。

translations.literal: the examinations valued literary composition alone, whereas schools also weighed conduct and character.
translations.idiomatic: the examinations valued literary composition alone, whereas schools also weighed conduct and character.

sentences.zh: 彼此相衡，難易迥別。

translations.literal: Weighed against each other, the difficulty differed vastly.
translations.idiomatic: Weighed against each other, the difficulty differed vastly.

sentences.zh: 人情莫不避難就易，當此時勢阽危，除興學外，更無養才濟時之術。

translations.literal: Human nature ever shuns difficulty for ease; at this time of perilous crisis, apart from promoting schools there was no other means of nurturing talent and serving the age.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature ever shuns difficulty for ease; at this time of perilous crisis, apart from promoting schools there was no other means of nurturing talent and serving the age.

sentences.zh: 或慮停罷科舉，士人競談西學，而中學無人肯講。

translations.literal: Some feared that if the examinations were suspended, scholars would all talk of Western learning while no one would study the Chinese classics.
translations.idiomatic: Some feared that if the examinations were suspended, scholars would all talk of Western learning while no one would study the Chinese classics.

sentences.zh: 現擬章程，於中學尤為注重。

translations.literal: The presently drafted regulations gave particular emphasis to middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: The presently drafted regulations gave particular emphasis to middle schools.

sentences.zh: 凡中國向有之經學、史學、文學、理學，無不包舉靡遺。

translations.literal: All the classics, history, literature, and Neo-Confucian philosophy that China had long possessed were encompassed without omission.
translations.idiomatic: All the classics, history, literature, and Neo-Confucian philosophy that China had long possessed were encompassed without omission.

sentences.zh: 科舉所講習者，學堂無不優為；

translations.literal: Whatever the examinations taught, schools did no less well;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the examinations taught, schools did no less well;

sentences.zh: 學堂所兼通者，科舉皆所未備。

translations.literal: whatever schools additionally mastered, the examinations had never provided.
translations.idiomatic: whatever schools additionally mastered, the examinations had never provided.

sentences.zh: 是取材於科舉，不如取材於學堂，彰彰明矣。

translations.literal: That recruiting talent from the examinations was inferior to recruiting from schools was abundantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: That recruiting talent from the examinations was inferior to recruiting from schools was abundantly clear.

sentences.zh: 或又慮學堂雖重積分法，分數定自教員，保無以愛憎而意為增損。

translations.literal: Others further feared that although schools relied on a cumulative grading system, since grades were set by teachers, there might be deliberate inflation or deflation out of personal favor or dislike.
translations.idiomatic: Others further feared that although schools relied on a cumulative grading system, since grades were set by teachers, there might be deliberate inflation or deflation out of personal favor or dislike.

sentences.zh: 不知功課優絀，當堂考驗。

translations.literal: One cannot know whether coursework is superior or inferior without testing it in class.
translations.idiomatic: Without in-class examinations, there is no way to tell strong work from weak.

sentences.zh: 教員即欲違眾徇私，而公論可憑，萬難掩飾。

translations.literal: Even if a teacher wished to defy public opinion and show favoritism, public judgment could be relied upon, and concealment would be extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Even a teacher inclined to favor pupils against the general view would find public scrutiny hard to evade.

sentences.zh: 臣等尚恐偶有此弊，故於中學考試，歸學政主持，督同道、府辦理。

translations.literal: Your ministers still feared this abuse might occasionally occur; therefore for middle-school examinations, responsibility was assigned to education commissioners to preside, with circuit intendants jointly supervising and prefectures handling the arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that such abuses might still arise, they placed middle-school examinations under education commissioners, with circuit officials and prefectures jointly overseeing the process.

sentences.zh: 高等學畢業，請簡放主考，會同督、撫、學政考試。

translations.literal: For graduation from higher schools, request the appointment of chief examiners to administer examinations jointly with governors-general, governors, and education commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Higher-school graduates were to be examined by imperially appointed chief examiners, acting together with governors-general, governors, and education commissioners.

sentences.zh: 大學畢業，請簡放總裁，會同學務大臣考試。

translations.literal: For university graduation, request the appointment of a chief superintendent to administer examinations jointly with the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: University graduates were to be examined by an imperially appointed chief superintendent, together with the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 不專憑本學堂所定分數。

translations.literal: Grades were not to rely solely on marks assigned by the home school.
translations.idiomatic: Final standing was not to depend on the home school's marks alone.

sentences.zh: 凡科舉掄才之法，已括諸學堂獎勵之中，實將科舉、學堂合併為一。

translations.literal: All methods by which the examinations selected talent had already been encompassed within school incentives; in effect the examinations and schools were merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: Every path by which the old examinations had chosen talent was now folded into school rewards—the two systems had effectively become one.

sentences.zh: 就事理論，必須科舉立時停罷，學堂辦法方有起色，經費方可設籌。

translations.literal: On principle, the examinations had to be stopped at once before school methods could improve and funds could be properly allocated.
translations.idiomatic: In logic, only an immediate end to the examinations could revive school practice and free up the money to sustain it.

sentences.zh: 惟此時各省學堂，未能遍設，已設學堂，辦理未盡合法，不欲遽議停罷科舉。

translations.literal: However, at this time schools in the provinces could not yet be established everywhere; those already established were not yet run entirely according to regulations, and they did not wish to propose abolishing the examinations hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Yet schools were still far from universal, and those that existed did not yet meet the rules—so an abrupt abolition of the examinations was not yet proposed.

sentences.zh: 然使一無舉動，天下未見朝廷有遞減以至停罷之明文，實不足風示海內士民，收振興學堂之效。

translations.literal: Yet if no action were taken, the empire would see no explicit decree from the court on gradual reduction leading to abolition, and this would truly be insufficient to instruct scholars and people throughout the realm and achieve the effect of reviving schools.
translations.idiomatic: To do nothing, however, would leave the country without a clear court promise of step-by-step reduction ending in abolition—hardly enough to move scholars nationwide toward the schools.

sentences.zh: 請查照臣之洞會同袁世凱原奏分科遞減之法，明降諭旨，從下屆丙午科起，每科遞減中額三分之一。

translations.literal: Request to follow the method of gradual reduction by examination category proposed in the original memorial jointly submitted by your minister Zhang Zhidong and Yuan Shikai, and issue an explicit edict: starting from the next Bingwu cycle, reduce provincial examination quotas by one-third each round.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the court adopt Zhang Zhidong and Yuan Shikai's earlier plan of staged cuts, and proclaim that from the next Bingwu examinations each round would trim provincial quotas by one-third.

sentences.zh: 一面照現定各學堂章程，從師範入手，責成各省實力舉行，至第三屆壬子科應減盡時，尚有十年。

translations.literal: Meanwhile, in accordance with established school regulations, begin with normal schools and hold each province responsible for earnest implementation; until the third Renzi cycle, when quotas should be fully reduced, there would still be ten years.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, under the new school rules, each province was to push normal schools first and carry the work out in earnest; ten years would remain before the third Renzi round, when quotas would reach zero.

sentences.zh: 計京、外開辦學堂，已逾十年以外，人才應已輩出。

translations.literal: Considering that schools in the capital and provinces had already been open for more than ten years, talent should already be emerging in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: By then schools at court and in the provinces would have been running for more than a decade, and trained men ought already to be coming forward.

sentences.zh: 天下士心專註學堂，籌措經費必立見踴躍。

translations.literal: Scholars throughout the realm would focus their hearts on schools, and fundraising would immediately become enthusiastic.
translations.idiomatic: Men of learning would turn their hopes to the schools, and money for them would flow in at once.

sentences.zh: 人人爭自濯磨，相率入學堂，求實在有用之學，氣象一新，人才自奮。

translations.literal: Everyone would strive to refine themselves, enter schools in succession, pursue genuinely useful learning—a renewed atmosphere, and talent naturally striving upward.
translations.idiomatic: People would polish themselves, flock into schools, and seek learning of real use; the mood would change, and ability would rise of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 轉弱為強，實基於此。

translations.literal: Turning weakness into strength would truly be founded on this.
translations.idiomatic: The road from weakness to strength would begin here.

sentences.zh: 」詔悉如所請。

translations.literal: An edict approved all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted everything they asked.

sentences.zh: 是為頒布奏定章程之期，時科舉未全廢止也。

translations.literal: This was the period when the memorial-approved regulations were promulgated; at the time the examinations had not yet been fully abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That was when the approved school code was issued—while the examination system still stood, though not for long.

sentences.zh: 迨三十一年，世凱、之洞會奏：「科舉一日不停，士人有僥倖得第之心，以分其砥礪實修之志。

translations.literal: By the thirty-first year, Yuan Shikai and Zhang Zhidong jointly memorialized: "As long as the examinations are not stopped for a single day, scholars will harbor hope of passing by luck, which divides their resolve to cultivate genuine self-improvement.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Yuan Shikai and Zhang Zhidong wrote together: "While the examinations continue even one day, scholars will keep hoping for a lucky pass, and that hope will split their will to train themselves in earnest.

sentences.zh: 民間相率觀望，私立學堂絕少。

translations.literal: Among the people all held back and waited; privately established schools were extremely few.
translations.idiomatic: The public hung back and watched; private schools were almost none.

sentences.zh: 如再遲十年甫停科舉，學堂有遷延之勢，人才非急切可求。

translations.literal: If the examinations were stopped only after another ten years' delay, schools would tend toward postponement, and talent could not be sought urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Wait another decade to end the examinations, and schools would keep slipping backward while the need for trained men grew urgent.

sentences.zh: 必須二十餘年後，始得多士之用。

translations.literal: More than twenty years would have to pass before sufficient scholars could be put to use.
translations.idiomatic: Not until twenty years had passed would the state have enough educated men to employ.

sentences.zh: 擬請宸衷獨斷，立罷科舉。

translations.literal: Propose requesting His Majesty's independent decision to abolish the examinations immediately.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore asked the throne to decide alone and abolish the examinations at once.

sentences.zh: 飭下各省督、撫、學政，學堂未辦者，從速提倡；

translations.literal: Order governors-general, governors, and education commissioners of all provinces: where schools had not yet been established, promote them with all speed;
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general, governors, and education commissioners in every province were commanded: where schools did not yet exist, establish them quickly;

sentences.zh: 已辦者，極力擴充。

translations.literal: where already established, expand them with full effort.
translations.idiomatic: where they already existed, expand them with all possible force.

sentences.zh: 學生之良莠，辦學人員之功過，認真考察，不得稍辭其責。

translations.literal: Conduct earnest inspection of the quality of students and the merit or fault of school personnel—none might shirk responsibility in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: Student quality and the performance of school staff were to be rigorously reviewed, and no one might evade that duty.

sentences.zh: 」遂詔自丙午科始，停止各省鄉、會試及歲、科試。

translations.literal: Then an edict ordered that from the Bingwu cycle onward, provincial and metropolitan examinations and annual and supplementary examinations in all provinces be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: from the Bingwu examinations onward, provincial and metropolitan tests, annual examinations, and supplementary examinations were abolished throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 尋諭各省學政專司考校學堂事務。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, education commissioners in all provinces were instructed to specialize in inspecting and managing school affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, provincial education commissioners were told to devote themselves to inspecting and administering schools.

sentences.zh: 於是沿襲千餘年之科舉制度，根本劃除。

translations.literal: Thus the examination system, inherited for more than a thousand years, was fundamentally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In this way a system more than a millennium old was cut out at the root.

sentences.zh: 嗣後學校日漸推廣，學術思想因之變遷，此其大關鍵也。

translations.literal: Thereafter schools gradually spread, and academic thought changed accordingly—this was the great turning point.
translations.idiomatic: Schools then spread year by year, and learning and thought shifted with them—the decisive hinge of the age.

sentences.zh: 是時學務之組織，尚有一重要之變更，則專設總理學務大臣也。

translations.literal: At this time there was still one important organizational change in educational affairs: the dedicated establishment of a Minister of Education to oversee all academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Educational administration also underwent a major change: the creation of a Minister of Education to govern the whole system.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，之洞言：「管學大臣既管京城大學堂，又管外省各學堂事務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Zhang Zhidong stated: "The Superintendent of Education both manages the Imperial University in the capital and manages school affairs in the outer provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Zhang Zhidong wrote: "The Superintendent of Education was charged both with the Imperial University in the capital and with schools in every province.

sentences.zh: 當此經營創始，條緒萬端，專任猶虞不給，兼綜更恐難周。

translations.literal: At this founding stage, with myriad threads of business, even exclusive dedication might not suffice—combining both duties fears falling short of comprehensiveness.
translations.idiomatic: In these first years of building, the work was endless; one man alone could barely manage it, and two great tasks together risked leaving both half done.

sentences.zh: 請於京師專設總理學務大臣，統轄全國學務。

translations.literal: Request establishing in the capital a dedicated Minister of Education to govern all educational affairs nationwide.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the capital appoint a Minister of Education devoted solely to governing national school affairs.

sentences.zh: 另設總監督一員，專管京師大學堂事務，受總理學務大臣節制考核，俾有專責。

translations.literal: Separately establish one Chief Supervisor dedicated to managing Imperial University affairs, subject to the Minister of Education's direction and evaluation, so that there would be clear responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Chief Supervisor should run the Imperial University alone, answerable to the Minister of Education for oversight and appraisal, so each office had a defined charge.

sentences.zh: 」詔允改管學大臣為學務大臣，並加派孫家鼐為學務大臣，命大理寺少卿張亨嘉充大學堂總監督。

translations.literal: An edict approved changing the Superintendent of Education to Minister of Education, additionally appointing Sun Jianai as Minister of Education, and ordering Zhang Hengjia, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, to serve as Chief Supervisor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed: the Superintendent of Education became Minister of Education; Sun Jianai was added to that post; and Zhang Hengjia, vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was named Chief Supervisor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 奏定章程，規定學校系統，足補欽定章程所未備。

translations.literal: The memorial-approved regulations defined the school system, sufficient to supplement what the imperially approved regulations had not provided.
translations.idiomatic: The approved regulations laid out the school system and filled gaps left by the earlier imperial code.

sentences.zh: 其分科及課目，較舊章亦多有變更。

translations.literal: Its divisions and curricula also changed in many respects from the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Its faculties and courses also diverged widely from the previous rules.

sentences.zh: 大學設通儒院及大學本科。

translations.literal: The university established an Academy of Universal Learning and undergraduate divisions.
translations.idiomatic: The university comprised an Academy of Universal Learning and an undergraduate college.

sentences.zh: 通儒院不講授，無規定課目。

translations.literal: The Academy of Universal Learning had no instruction and no prescribed curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: The Academy of Universal Learning offered no lectures and set no fixed courses.

sentences.zh: 大學本科分科八。

translations.literal: The university undergraduate program was divided into eight faculties.
translations.idiomatic: Undergraduate study was organized into eight faculties.

sentences.zh: 曰經學科，分十一門：周易、尚書、毛詩、春秋左傳、春秋三傳、周禮、儀禮、禮記、論語、孟子，附理學。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Classical Studies, divided into eleven sections: Book of Changes, Book of Documents, Mao's Classic of Poetry, Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites of Zhou, Ceremonies and Rites, Book of Rites, Analects, Mencius, with Neo-Confucian philosophy attached.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Classical Studies with eleven branches: Changes, Documents, Mao's Poetry, the Zuo Commentary, the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites of Zhou, Ceremonies and Rites, the Book of Rites, the Analects, Mencius, and Neo-Confucian philosophy.

sentences.zh: 曰政法科，分二門：政治、法律。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Politics and Law, divided into two sections: politics and law.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Politics and Law with two branches: politics and law.

sentences.zh: 曰文學科，分九門：中國史、萬國史、中外地理、中國文學、英國文學、法國文學、俄國文學、德國文學、日本國文學。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Letters, divided into nine sections: Chinese history, world history, Chinese and foreign geography, Chinese literature, English literature, French literature, Russian literature, German literature, Japanese literature.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Letters with nine branches: Chinese history, world history, Chinese and foreign geography, Chinese literature, and the literatures of England, France, Russia, Germany, and Japan.

sentences.zh: 曰醫科，分二門：醫學、藥學。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Medicine, divided into two sections: medicine and pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Medicine with two branches: medicine and pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 曰格致科，分六門：算學、星學、物理、化學、動植物、地質。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Natural Sciences, divided into six sections: mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry, zoology and botany, geology.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Natural Sciences with six branches: mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry, zoology and botany, and geology.

sentences.zh: 曰農科，分四門：農學、農藝化學、林學、獸醫。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Agriculture, divided into four sections: agricultural science, agricultural chemistry, forestry, veterinary medicine.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Agriculture with four branches: agricultural science, agricultural chemistry, forestry, and veterinary medicine.

sentences.zh: 曰工科，分九門：土木、機器、造船、造兵器、電氣、建築、應用化學、火藥、採礦冶金。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Engineering, divided into nine sections: civil engineering, mechanical engineering, shipbuilding, arms manufacture, electrical engineering, architecture, applied chemistry, explosives, mining and metallurgy.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Engineering with nine branches: civil engineering, mechanical engineering, shipbuilding, arms manufacture, electrical engineering, architecture, applied chemistry, explosives, and mining and metallurgy.

sentences.zh: 曰商科，分三門：銀行及保險、貿易及販運、關稅。

translations.literal: Called the Faculty of Commerce, divided into three sections: banking and insurance, trade and distribution, customs and tariffs.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Faculty of Commerce with three branches: banking and insurance, trade and distribution, and customs and tariffs.

sentences.zh: 各專一門。

translations.literal: Each specialized in one section.
translations.idiomatic: Each student was to concentrate on a single branch.

sentences.zh: 經學原兼習一兩經者聽。

translations.literal: In classical studies, those who originally studied one or two classics together were permitted to continue.
translations.idiomatic: In classical studies, students who had already combined one or two classics might keep doing so.

sentences.zh: 各學科分主課、補助課。

translations.literal: Each faculty divided courses into major subjects and auxiliary subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Every faculty distinguished major courses from supporting courses.

sentences.zh: 三年畢業。

translations.literal: Three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course of study lasted three years.

sentences.zh: 惟政治、醫學四年畢業。

translations.literal: Only politics and medicine required four years.
translations.idiomatic: Politics and medicine alone required four years.

sentences.zh: 高等學與大學豫備科性質相同。

translations.literal: Higher schools and university preparatory departments were of the same nature.
translations.idiomatic: Higher schools and the university preparatory course were equivalent in purpose.

sentences.zh: 學科分三類：第一類為豫備入經學、政法、文學、商科等大學者治之，第二類為豫備入格致、農、工等科大學者治之，第三類為豫備入醫科大學者治之。

translations.literal: Subjects were divided into three categories: the first for those preparing to enter university faculties of classical studies, politics and law, letters, and commerce; the second for those preparing to enter faculties of natural sciences, agriculture, and engineering; the third for those preparing to enter the medical faculty.
translations.idiomatic: Curricula fell into three tracks: the first for students bound for classical studies, politics and law, letters, or commerce; the second for natural sciences, agriculture, or engineering; the third for medicine.

sentences.zh: 學科除人倫道德、經學大義、中國文學、外國語、體操各類共同外，第一類課歷史、地理、辨學、法學、理財，第二類課算學、物理、化學、地質、礦物、圖畫，第三類課蠟丁語、算學、物理、化學、動物、植物。

translations.literal: Beyond ethics, essentials of classical studies, Chinese literature, foreign languages, and gymnastics common to all categories: the first category taught history, geography, logic, jurisprudence, and finance; the second taught mathematics, physics, chemistry, geology, mineralogy, and drawing; the third taught Latin, mathematics, physics, chemistry, zoology, and botany.
translations.idiomatic: All three tracks shared ethics, classical essentials, Chinese literature, foreign languages, and gymnastics; the first added history, geography, logic, law, and finance; the second added mathematics, physics, chemistry, geology, mineralogy, and drawing; the third added Latin, mathematics, physics, chemistry, zoology, and botany.

sentences.zh: 其有志入某科某門者，得缺科目或加課他科目，分通習、主課。

translations.literal: Those intending to enter a particular faculty and section might omit certain subjects or add others, divided into general courses and major courses.
translations.idiomatic: Students aiming at a given faculty and branch might drop some subjects or add others, classed as general or major courses.

sentences.zh: 三年畢業。

translations.literal: Three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course lasted three years.

sentences.zh: 中學科目：修身、讀經、講經、中國文學、外國語、歷史、地理、算學、博物、物理及化學、法制及理財、圖畫、體操。

translations.literal: Middle school subjects: moral cultivation, Scripture reading, Scripture exposition, Chinese literature, foreign languages, history, geography, mathematics, natural history, physics and chemistry, law and finance, drawing, gymnastics.
translations.idiomatic: Middle schools taught moral cultivation, Scripture reading and exposition, Chinese literature, foreign languages, history, geography, mathematics, natural history, physics and chemistry, law and finance, drawing, and gymnastics.

sentences.zh: 五年畢業。

translations.literal: Five years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course lasted five years.

sentences.zh: 高等小學科目：修身、讀經、講經、中國文學、算術、中國歷史、地理、格致、圖畫、體操。

translations.literal: Higher primary school subjects: moral cultivation, Scripture reading, Scripture exposition, Chinese literature, arithmetic, Chinese history, geography, natural sciences, drawing, gymnastics.
translations.idiomatic: Higher primary schools taught moral cultivation, Scripture reading and exposition, Chinese literature, arithmetic, Chinese history, geography, natural sciences, drawing, and gymnastics.

sentences.zh: 視地方情形，可加授手工、農、商業等科目。

translations.literal: Depending on local conditions, handicrafts, agriculture, commerce, and other subjects might be added.
translations.idiomatic: Local conditions might warrant added instruction in handicrafts, farming, commerce, or other subjects.

sentences.zh: 四年畢業。

translations.literal: Four years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course lasted four years.

sentences.zh: 初等小學科目：修身、讀經、講經、中國文學、算術、歷史、地理、格致、體操，為完全科。

translations.literal: Lower primary school subjects: moral cultivation, Scripture reading, Scripture exposition, Chinese literature, arithmetic, history, geography, natural sciences, gymnastics—comprising the full curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: Lower primary schools taught moral cultivation, Scripture reading and exposition, Chinese literature, arithmetic, history, geography, natural sciences, and gymnastics as the full course.

sentences.zh: 視地方情形，可加授圖畫、手工之一二科目。

translations.literal: Depending on local conditions, one or two subjects such as drawing or handicrafts might be added.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing, handicrafts, or one or two similar subjects might be added according to local need.

sentences.zh: 其鄉民貧瘠、師儒缺少地方，得量從簡略，修身、讀經合為一科，中國文學科，歷史、地理、格致合為一科，算術、體操，為簡易科。

translations.literal: Where villages were poor and teachers scarce, simplification was permitted: moral cultivation and Scripture reading combined into one subject; Chinese literature as one subject; history, geography, and natural sciences combined into one subject; arithmetic and gymnastics—constituting the simplified curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: In poor villages with too few teachers, a reduced course was allowed: moral cultivation and Scripture reading as one subject, Chinese literature as another, history-geography-natural sciences as a third, and arithmetic and gymnastics—together forming the simplified track.

sentences.zh: 五年畢業。

translations.literal: Five years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: That course also lasted five years.

sentences.zh: 中、小學科目，不外普通教育之學科。

translations.literal: Middle and primary school subjects were nothing beyond the disciplines of general education.
translations.idiomatic: Middle and primary schools taught only the ordinary branches of general education.

sentences.zh: 其特殊者，則讀經、講經一科也。

translations.literal: What was special was the single subject of Scripture reading and exposition.
translations.idiomatic: The distinctive feature was the combined course in reading and explaining the classics.

sentences.zh: 學務綱要載中、小學宜注意讀經以存聖教一節，其言曰：「外國學堂有宗教一門，中國之經書即是中國之宗教。

translations.literal: The Educational Outline stated a section on how middle and primary schools should emphasize Scripture reading to preserve the sacred teaching, which said: "Foreign schools have a subject of religion; China's classics are China's religion.
translations.idiomatic: The Educational Outline urged middle and primary schools to keep Scripture reading in order to preserve the sacred teaching, arguing: "Western schools teach religion; in China the classics are religion.

sentences.zh: 學堂不讀經，則是堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周公、孔子之道，所謂三綱五常，盡行廢絕，中國必不能立國。

translations.literal: If schools do not read the classics, then the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—the so-called Three Bonds and Five Constants—would be entirely abandoned, and China could not stand as a nation.
translations.idiomatic: Without classic reading in the schools, the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—the Three Bonds and Five Constants—would be cast off altogether, and China could not endure as a state.

sentences.zh: 無論學生將來所執何業，即由小學改業者，必須曾誦經書之要言，略聞聖教之要義，以定其心性，正其本源。

translations.literal: Whatever occupation students might later pursue, even those who left school after primary school, they must have recited essential passages of the classics and gained some knowledge of the sacred teaching's core meaning, to fix their character and rectify their foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever trade a pupil might later follow, even if he left after primary school, he had to have recited the classics' chief passages and grasped the sacred teaching's essentials, so that character and root might be set right.

sentences.zh: 惟學堂科學較繁，晷刻有限，概令全讀十三經，精力日力斷斷不給。

translations.literal: However, school science was relatively extensive and time limited—requiring the complete reading of all Thirteen Classics would clearly exceed students' energy and daily capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet modern subjects were many and hours few; to read all Thirteen Classics in full would plainly exceed what students could bear.

sentences.zh: 茲擇切要各經，分配中、小學堂。

translations.literal: Now the most essential classics were selected and assigned to middle and primary schools.
translations.idiomatic: The most necessary classics were therefore chosen and distributed through middle and primary schools.

sentences.zh: 若卷帙繁重之禮記、周禮，止選讀通儒節本，儀禮止選讀最要一篇。

translations.literal: For voluminous works like the Book of Rites and Rites of Zhou, only abridged editions by eminent scholars were selected for reading; for Ceremonies and Rites, only the most essential chapter was selected.
translations.idiomatic: Bulky texts such as the Book of Rites and Rites of Zhou were read in scholarly abridgments; Ceremonies and Rites was limited to its most important section.

sentences.zh: 自初等小學第一年日讀約四十字起，至中學日讀約二百字為止，大率小學每日以一點鐘讀經，一點鐘挑背淺解。

translations.literal: Starting from approximately forty characters per day in the first year of lower primary school, up to approximately two hundred characters per day in middle school; generally in primary school one hour daily for Scripture reading and one hour for recitation and shallow explication.
translations.idiomatic: Daily reading began at about forty characters in the first year of lower primary school and rose to about two hundred in middle school; in primary grades, one hour was for reading and one for recitation with brief explanation.

sentences.zh: 中學每星期以六點鐘讀經，三點鐘挑背講解。

translations.literal: In middle school, six hours per week for Scripture reading and three hours for recitation and exposition.
translations.idiomatic: Middle schools allotted six hours a week to reading and three to recitation and explanation.

sentences.zh: 溫經每日半點鐘，歸自習時督課。

translations.literal: Review of classics half an hour daily, supervised during self-study.
translations.idiomatic: Half an hour each day was set aside for review, checked during self-study.

sentences.zh: 學生並不過勞，亦無礙講習西學之日力。

translations.literal: Students would not be overworked, nor would it interfere with time for Western learning.
translations.idiomatic: The burden would not overtax pupils, nor would it crowd out Western studies.

sentences.zh: 計中學畢業，已讀過孝經、四書、易、書、詩、左傳及禮記、周禮、儀禮節本十經，並通大義。

translations.literal: By middle school graduation, students would have read the Classic of Filial Piety, the Four Books, Changes, Documents, Poetry, Zuo Commentary, and abridged editions of the Book of Rites, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonies and Rites—ten classics in all—and understood their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: By middle-school graduation a student would have read the Classic of Filial Piety, the Four Books, Changes, Documents, Poetry, the Zuo Commentary, and abridgments of the Book of Rites, Rites of Zhou, and Ceremonies and Rites—ten classics in all—and grasped their main import.

sentences.zh: 較之向來書塾、書院所讀所解，已為加多。

translations.literal: Compared with what was read and understood in traditional village schools and academies, this was already greater.
translations.idiomatic: That was already more than village schools and private academies had commonly read and explained.

sentences.zh: 不惟聖經不至廢墜，且經學從此更可昌明。

translations.literal: Not only would the sacred classics not fall into neglect, but classical studies from this could further flourish.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred texts would not be abandoned; classical learning might even flourish anew.

sentences.zh: 」其立論甚正，可考見當時之風氣焉。

translations.literal: Its reasoning was quite sound, from which one may discern the spirit of the times.
translations.idiomatic: The argument was sound enough to reveal the temper of the age.

sentences.zh: 齋蒙養院意在合蒙養、家教為一，輔助家庭教育，兼包括女學。

translations.literal: The purpose of kindergartens was to unite early nurture and home education, assist home education, and include girls' schools as well.
translations.idiomatic: Kindergartens were meant to join early nurture with home instruction, support family education, and embrace girls' schools too.

sentences.zh: 直系學堂外，並詳訂師範及實業學堂專章。

translations.literal: Beyond schools in the direct line, detailed chapters were also drawn up for normal schools and vocational schools.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the main ladder of schools, separate detailed chapters covered normal and vocational schools.

sentences.zh: 其大異於舊章者，為優級師範學堂。

translations.literal: What differed greatly from the old regulations was the higher normal school.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest departure from earlier rules was the higher normal school.

sentences.zh: 學科分三節：一曰公共科，以補中學之不足，為本科之豫備。

translations.literal: Subjects were divided into three stages: first, the common curriculum, to supplement what middle school did not cover and serve as preparation for the undergraduate program.
translations.idiomatic: Its course fell into three stages: a common curriculum to fill gaps left by middle school and prepare for the main program.

sentences.zh: 科目：人倫道德、群經源流、中國文學、東語、英語、辨學、算學、體操。

translations.literal: Subjects: ethics, origins of the classics, Chinese literature, Japanese, English, logic, mathematics, gymnastics.
translations.idiomatic: That stage included ethics, origins of the classics, Chinese literature, Japanese, English, logic, mathematics, and gymnastics.

sentences.zh: 一年畢業。

translations.literal: One year to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: It lasted one year.

sentences.zh: 二曰分類科，凡四類：第一類以中國文學、外國語為主。

translations.literal: Second, the classified curriculum, four categories in all: the first category focused on Chinese literature and foreign languages.
translations.idiomatic: Second came the classified curriculum in four tracks; the first emphasized Chinese literature and foreign languages.

sentences.zh: 第二類以地理、歷史為主。

translations.literal: The second category focused on geography and history.
translations.idiomatic: The second emphasized geography and history.

sentences.zh: 第三類以算學、物理、化學為主。

translations.literal: The third category focused on mathematics, physics, and chemistry.
translations.idiomatic: The third emphasized mathematics, physics, and chemistry.

sentences.zh: 第四類以動植物、礦物、生理為主。

translations.literal: The fourth category focused on zoology and botany, mineralogy, and physiology.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth emphasized zoology and botany, mineralogy, and physiology.

sentences.zh: 科目除人倫道德、經學大義、中國文學、教育心理、體操各類共同外，第一類課周秦諸子、英語、德語或法語、辨學、生物、生理。

translations.literal: Beyond ethics, essentials of classical studies, Chinese literature, educational psychology, and gymnastics common to all categories: the first category taught pre-Qin masters, English, German or French, logic, biology, and physiology.
translations.idiomatic: All four tracks shared ethics, classical essentials, Chinese literature, educational psychology, and gymnastics; the first added pre-Qin masters, English, German or French, logic, biology, and physiology.

sentences.zh: 第二類課地理、歷史、法制、理財、英語、生物。

translations.literal: The second category taught geography, history, law, finance, English, and biology.
translations.idiomatic: The second added geography, history, law, finance, English, and biology.

sentences.zh: 第三類課算學、物理、化學、英語、圖畫、手工。

translations.literal: The third category taught mathematics, physics, chemistry, English, drawing, and handicrafts.
translations.idiomatic: The third added mathematics, physics, chemistry, English, drawing, and handicrafts.

sentences.zh: 第四類課植物、動物、生理、礦物、地學、農學、英語、圖畫。

translations.literal: The fourth category taught botany, zoology, physiology, mineralogy, earth science, agricultural science, English, and drawing.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth added botany, zoology, physiology, mineralogy, earth science, agricultural science, English, and drawing.

sentences.zh: 分通習、主課，均三年畢業。

translations.literal: Divided into general courses and major courses; all three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: Courses were split between general and major subjects, each track running three years.

sentences.zh: 三曰加習科，於分類科畢業，擇教育重要數門，加習一年，以資深造。

translations.literal: Third, the supplementary curriculum: upon graduating from the classified curriculum, select several important subjects in education for an additional year of study, to provide advanced training.
translations.idiomatic: Third came a supplementary year after the classified course, devoted to a few key subjects in education for deeper training.

sentences.zh: 科目：人倫道德、教育學、教育制度、教育政令機關、美學、實驗心理、學校衛生、專科教育、兒童研究、教育演習，並增入教授實事練習。

translations.literal: Subjects: ethics, education, educational systems, educational policy and administrative organs, aesthetics, experimental psychology, school hygiene, specialized education, child study, educational practice, with the addition of practical teaching exercises.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects included ethics, education, school systems, educational policy and administration, aesthetics, experimental psychology, school hygiene, specialized education, child study, and teaching practice, plus practical classroom training.

sentences.zh: 優級師範附屬中學堂、小學堂。

translations.literal: Higher normal schools had affiliated middle schools and primary schools.
translations.idiomatic: Each higher normal school had its own affiliated middle and primary schools.

sentences.zh: 初級師範學科程度，與中學略同。

translations.literal: The academic level of elementary normal schools was roughly the same as middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary normal schools were set at roughly the same academic level as middle schools.

sentences.zh: 完全科學科，於中學科目外，增教育學、習字。

translations.literal: For the full curriculum, beyond middle-school subjects, education and penmanship were added.
translations.idiomatic: The full course added education and penmanship to the standard middle-school subjects.

sentences.zh: 視地方情形，可加外國語，手工，農、工業之一科目或數科目。

translations.literal: Depending on local conditions, one or several subjects could be added from among foreign languages, handicrafts, and agriculture or industry.
translations.idiomatic: Local conditions might warrant adding foreign languages, handicrafts, or one or more agricultural or industrial subjects.

sentences.zh: 五年畢業。

translations.literal: Five years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course ran five years.

sentences.zh: 初級師範附屬小學堂。

translations.literal: Elementary normal schools had affiliated primary schools.
translations.idiomatic: Each elementary normal school also maintained an affiliated primary school.

sentences.zh: 實業學堂之種類，曰實業教員講習所，曰高等農、工、商實業學堂，曰中等農、工、商實業學堂，曰初等農、工、商實業學堂，及高等、中等、初等商船學堂，曰實業補習普通學堂，曰藝徒學堂。

translations.literal: Types of vocational schools included: institutes for training vocational teachers; higher agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools; middle-level agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools; elementary agricultural, industrial, and commercial vocational schools; higher, middle, and elementary merchant-marine schools; general supplementary vocational schools; and apprentice schools.
translations.idiomatic: Vocational schools fell into several types: teacher-training institutes; higher, middle, and elementary schools of agriculture, industry, and commerce; higher, middle, and elementary merchant-marine schools; general supplementary vocational schools; and apprentice schools.

sentences.zh: 實業教員講習所，以備教成各項實業學堂之教習。

translations.literal: The institutes for training vocational teachers were to prepare instructors for the various vocational schools.
translations.idiomatic: Teacher-training institutes existed to prepare instructors for every kind of vocational school.

sentences.zh: 分農、商、工三種，農業、商業教員講習所，除人倫道德、英語、教育、教授法、體操為共同學科外，農業課算學及測量氣象、農業汎論、農業化學、農具、土壤、肥料、耕種、畜產、園藝、昆蟲、獸醫、水產、森林、農產製造、農業理財實習；

translations.literal: Divided into three types: agricultural, commercial, and industrial. For agricultural and commercial teacher-training institutes, beyond the common subjects of ethics, English, education, teaching methods, and gymnastics, agriculture taught mathematics and surveying and meteorology, general agriculture, agricultural chemistry, farm implements, soil, fertilizers, cultivation, animal husbandry, horticulture, entomology, veterinary medicine, aquatic products, forestry, agricultural product processing, and practical agricultural finance.
translations.idiomatic: There were agricultural, commercial, and industrial tracks. Agricultural and commercial teacher-training shared ethics, English, education, teaching methods, and gymnastics; agriculture then added mathematics, surveying and meteorology, general agriculture, agricultural chemistry, farm tools, soil, fertilizers, cultivation, animal husbandry, horticulture, entomology, veterinary medicine, fisheries, forestry, farm-product processing, and practical agricultural finance.

sentences.zh: 商業課應用化學、應用物理、商業作文、商業算術、商業地理、商業歷史、簿記、商品、商業理財、商業實踐。

translations.literal: Commerce taught applied chemistry, applied physics, commercial composition, commercial arithmetic, commercial geography, commercial history, bookkeeping, commodities, commercial finance, and commercial practice.
translations.idiomatic: Commerce added applied chemistry and physics, commercial writing and arithmetic, commercial geography and history, bookkeeping, commodities, commercial finance, and practical business work.

sentences.zh: 均二年畢業。

translations.literal: Both required two years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: Both tracks lasted two years.

sentences.zh: 工業教員講習所，置完全科及簡易科。

translations.literal: Industrial teacher-training institutes had full and simplified curricula.
translations.idiomatic: Industrial teacher-training offered full and abbreviated courses.

sentences.zh: 完全科凡六：曰金工科、木工科、染織科、窯業科、應用化學科、工業圖樣科。

translations.literal: The full curriculum had six divisions: metallurgy, woodworking, dyeing and weaving, ceramics, applied chemistry, and industrial drafting.
translations.idiomatic: The full course had six divisions: metallurgy, woodworking, dyeing and weaving, ceramics, applied chemistry, and industrial drafting.

sentences.zh: 除人倫道德、算學、物理、化學、圖畫、工業理財、工業衛生、機器製圖實習、英語、教育、教授法、體操為共同學科外，金工科課無機化學、應用力學、工場用具及製造法、電氣工業大意、發動機。

translations.literal: Beyond the common subjects of ethics, mathematics, physics, chemistry, drawing, industrial finance, industrial hygiene, practical machine drafting, English, education, teaching methods, and gymnastics, metallurgy taught inorganic chemistry, applied mechanics, workshop tools and manufacturing methods, essentials of electrical industry, and engines.
translations.idiomatic: All six divisions shared ethics, mathematics, physics, chemistry, drawing, industrial finance and hygiene, machine-drafting practice, English, education, teaching methods, and gymnastics; metallurgy then added inorganic chemistry, applied mechanics, workshop tools and manufacturing, essentials of electrical industry, and engines.

sentences.zh: 木工科課無機化學、應用力學、工場用具及製造法、構造用材料、傢具及建築流派、房屋構造、衛生、建築製圖及意匠。

translations.literal: Woodworking taught inorganic chemistry, applied mechanics, workshop tools and manufacturing methods, construction materials, furniture and architectural styles, building construction, sanitation, architectural drafting and design.
translations.idiomatic: Woodworking added inorganic chemistry, applied mechanics, workshop tools and manufacturing, construction materials, furniture and architectural styles, building construction, sanitation, and architectural drafting and design.

sentences.zh: 染織科課一切器用化學、應用機器、定性分析、工業分析、染色配色、機織及意匠。

translations.literal: Dyeing and weaving taught general appliance chemistry, applied machinery, qualitative analysis, industrial analysis, dyeing and color matching, and mechanical weaving and design.
translations.idiomatic: Dyeing and weaving added general applied chemistry, applied machinery, qualitative and industrial analysis, dyeing and color matching, and mechanical weaving and design.

sentences.zh: 窯業科課一切應用化學、應用機器、定性分析、工業分析、窯業品製造。

translations.literal: Ceramics taught general applied chemistry, applied machinery, qualitative analysis, industrial analysis, and ceramic product manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Ceramics added general applied chemistry, applied machinery, qualitative and industrial analysis, and ceramic manufacture.

sentences.zh: 應用化學科課一切應用化學、機器、電鑄及電礦。

translations.literal: Applied chemistry taught general applied chemistry, machinery, electrotyping, and electroplating.
translations.idiomatic: Applied chemistry added general applied chemistry, machinery, electrotyping, and electroplating.

sentences.zh: 工業圖樣科課圖樣、材料。

translations.literal: Industrial drafting taught drafting and materials.
translations.idiomatic: Industrial drafting covered drafting and materials.

sentences.zh: 均三年畢業。

translations.literal: All required three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: All full divisions ran three years.

sentences.zh: 簡易科分金工、木工、染色、機織、陶器、漆工六科。

translations.literal: The simplified curriculum had six divisions: metalwork, woodworking, dyeing, mechanical weaving, pottery, and lacquerwork.
translations.idiomatic: The abbreviated course had six divisions: metalwork, woodworking, dyeing, mechanical weaving, pottery, and lacquerwork.

sentences.zh: 課目較略。

translations.literal: The subjects were somewhat abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: Its subjects were more limited.

sentences.zh: 一年畢業。

translations.literal: One year to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: It lasted one year.

sentences.zh: 高等實業學堂程度視高等學堂，分豫科、本科。

translations.literal: Higher vocational schools were on a par with higher schools, divided into preparatory and undergraduate programs.
translations.idiomatic: Higher vocational schools matched higher schools in level and were split into preparatory and undergraduate programs.

sentences.zh: 豫科授以各科普通基本功課。

translations.literal: The preparatory program taught basic general courses in each field.
translations.idiomatic: The preparatory year taught the basic general courses of each field.

sentences.zh: 一年畢業。

translations.literal: One year to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: It lasted one year.

sentences.zh: 高等農業本科凡三：曰農學科，曰林學科，曰獸醫學科。

translations.literal: The undergraduate program of higher agricultural schools had three divisions: agriculture, forestry, and veterinary medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Higher agricultural schools offered three undergraduate divisions: agriculture, forestry, and veterinary medicine.

sentences.zh: 高等工業分科十三：曰應用化學科，曰染色科，曰機織科，曰建築科，曰窯業科，曰機器科，曰電器科，曰電氣化學科，曰土木科，曰礦業科，曰造船科，曰漆工科，曰圖稿繪畫科，各授以本科原理、原則、應用方法及補助科目，多者至三十餘門，得斟酌地方情形，擇合宜數科設之。

translations.literal: Higher industrial schools had thirteen divisions: applied chemistry, dyeing, mechanical weaving, architecture, ceramics, machinery, electrical appliances, electrochemistry, civil engineering, mining, shipbuilding, lacquerwork, and technical drawing and painting. Each taught undergraduate principles, fundamentals, applied methods, and supplementary subjects, some exceeding thirty courses in all. Depending on local conditions, an appropriate number of divisions could be selected and established.
translations.idiomatic: Higher industrial schools had thirteen divisions—applied chemistry, dyeing, mechanical weaving, architecture, ceramics, machinery, electrical appliances, electrochemistry, civil engineering, mining, shipbuilding, lacquerwork, and technical drawing and painting—each teaching principles, fundamentals, applied methods, and supporting subjects, sometimes more than thirty in all. Local conditions determined how many divisions were actually established.

sentences.zh: 均三年畢業。

translations.literal: All required three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: All ran three years.

sentences.zh: 中等實業學堂程度視中學堂，亦分豫科、本科，課目較高等為略。

translations.literal: Middle vocational schools were on a par with middle schools, also divided into preparatory and undergraduate programs, with subjects somewhat more limited than the higher level.
translations.idiomatic: Middle vocational schools matched middle schools in level, with preparatory and undergraduate stages and a narrower curriculum than the higher schools.

sentences.zh: 初等實業學堂程度視高等小學堂，分普通、實習兩種科目。

translations.literal: Elementary vocational schools were on a par with higher primary schools, with subjects divided into general and practical types.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary vocational schools matched higher primary schools and divided their subjects into general and practical courses.

sentences.zh: 均三年畢業。

translations.literal: All required three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: Both tracks lasted three years.

sentences.zh: 商船學堂亦分三等，以授航海機關之學術及駕運商船之知識技術。

translations.literal: Merchant-marine schools were also divided into three levels, to teach the science of navigation and machinery and the knowledge and skills needed to command and operate merchant vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant-marine schools also had three levels, teaching navigation, marine engineering, and the knowledge and skills needed to command merchant ships.

sentences.zh: 五年或三年畢業。

translations.literal: Five or three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: Courses ran either five or three years.

sentences.zh: 實業補習普通學堂，以簡易教法授實業必須之知識技能，並補習小學科目。

translations.literal: General supplementary vocational schools used simplified methods to teach knowledge and skills essential to vocational work, while also supplementing primary-school subjects.
translations.idiomatic: General supplementary vocational schools used simplified methods to teach essential vocational skills while also making up primary-school subjects.

sentences.zh: 藝徒學堂，授平等程度之工築技術，俾成良善工匠，均可於中、小學堂便宜附設。

translations.literal: Apprentice schools taught technical skills at a uniform level to produce skilled craftsmen; any of these could be conveniently established as adjuncts to middle or primary schools.
translations.idiomatic: Apprentice schools taught trades at a uniform level to train skilled craftsmen and could conveniently be attached to middle or primary schools.

sentences.zh: 其不在學堂系統內者，曰譯學館，曰進士館。

translations.literal: Those outside the school system included the School of Translation and the Jinshi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the main school ladder stood the School of Translation and the Jinshi Hall.

sentences.zh: 先是同文館併入大學堂，設英、法、俄、德、日本五國語文專科，後由大學分出，名譯學館。

translations.literal: Previously the Tongwen Guan had been merged into the Imperial University, establishing specialized programs in English, French, Russian, German, and Japanese; later it was separated from the university and named the School of Translation.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongwen Guan had first been merged into the Imperial University as specialized programs in English, French, Russian, German, and Japanese; later it was split off again as the School of Translation.

sentences.zh: 仍設英、法、俄、德、日本文各一科，無論習何國文，皆須習普通及專門學。

translations.literal: English, French, Russian, German, and Japanese each still had one program; regardless of which language was studied, students had to take both general and specialized courses.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five languages still had its own program, but every student, whatever language he studied, had to take both general and specialized courses.

sentences.zh: 普通科目：人倫道德、中國文學、歷史、地理、算學、博物、物理及化學、圖畫、體操。

translations.literal: General subjects: ethics, Chinese literature, history, geography, mathematics, natural history, physics and chemistry, drawing, and gymnastics.
translations.idiomatic: General subjects included ethics, Chinese literature, history, geography, mathematics, natural history, physics and chemistry, drawing, and gymnastics.

sentences.zh: 專門科目：交涉、理財、教育。

translations.literal: Specialized subjects: diplomacy, finance, and education.
translations.idiomatic: Specialized subjects covered diplomacy, finance, and education.

sentences.zh: 五年畢業。

translations.literal: Five years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course ran five years.

sentences.zh: 進士館令新進士用翰林部屬、中書者，入館肄業，講求實用之學。

translations.literal: The Jinshi Hall ordered new jinshi who had been appointed to Hanlin Academy posts or as zhongshu to enter the hall for study, seeking practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinshi Hall required newly minted jinshi appointed to Hanlin posts or as secretaries to enter for study in practical subjects.

sentences.zh: 課目：史學、地理、教育、法學、理財、交涉、兵政、農政、工政、商政、格致。

translations.literal: Subjects: history, geography, education, law, finance, diplomacy, military administration, agricultural administration, industrial administration, commercial administration, and general science.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects included history, geography, education, law, finance, diplomacy, military administration, agricultural administration, industrial administration, commercial administration, and general science.

sentences.zh: 得選習農、工、商、兵之一科或兩科。

translations.literal: Students could choose to study one or two of agriculture, industry, commerce, or military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Students might elect one or two of agriculture, industry, commerce, or military affairs.

sentences.zh: 西文、東文、算學、體操為隨意科。

translations.literal: Western languages, Eastern languages, mathematics, and gymnastics were optional subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Western languages, Eastern languages, mathematics, and gymnastics were optional.

sentences.zh: 三年畢業。

translations.literal: Three years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course ran three years.

sentences.zh: 各學堂管理通則之規定，與舊章大體相同。

translations.literal: The general regulations for administering schools were largely the same as the old rules.
translations.idiomatic: The general rules for running schools largely followed the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 月朔，監督、教員集諸生禮堂，宣讀聖諭廣訓一條。

translations.literal: On the first day of each month, the superintendent and teachers assembled the students in the hall and read aloud one entry from the Sacred Edict and Amplified Instructions.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of each month the superintendent and teachers gathered the students in the hall and read one passage from the Sacred Edict and Amplified Instructions.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇上萬壽節，至聖先師孔子誕日，春、秋上丁釋奠，為慶祝日。

translations.literal: The birthdays of the Empress Dowager and the Emperor, the birthday of Confucius, and the spring and autumn shangding sacrificial ceremonies were celebrated days.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated days included the birthdays of the Empress Dowager and the Emperor, the birthday of Confucius, and the spring and autumn shangding sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 堂中各員率學生至萬歲牌前或聖人位前行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: All staff in the hall led the students before the Long-Life tablets or the seat of the Sage and performed the three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: All staff led the students before the Long-Life tablets or Confucius's seat and performed the three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 畢，各員西鄉立，學生向各員行三揖禮，退。

translations.literal: When finished, the staff stood facing west, the students bowed to them three times with joined hands, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was done, the staff stood facing west while the students bowed to them three times and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 開學、散學或畢業，率學生至萬歲牌前、聖人位前行禮如儀。

translations.literal: At the opening, closing, or graduation of school, students were led before the Long-Life tablets and the seat of the Sage to perform the rites as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: At opening, closing, or graduation, students were led before the Long-Life tablets and Confucius's seat to perform the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 學生向監督、教員行一跪三叩禮。

translations.literal: Students performed one kneeling and three prostrations before the superintendent and teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Students then performed one kneeling and three prostrations before the superintendent and teachers.

sentences.zh: 監督等施訓語，乃散。

translations.literal: The superintendent and others delivered admonitions, and then the assembly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent and others gave admonitions, and the assembly broke up.

sentences.zh: 月朔，率學生至聖人位前行禮如儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of each month, students were led before the seat of the Sage to perform the rites as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of each month students were led before Confucius's seat to perform the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 每日講堂授課，多者不得過六小時。

translations.literal: Daily classroom instruction could not exceed six hours at most.
translations.idiomatic: Daily classroom instruction could not exceed six hours.

sentences.zh: 房、虛、星、昴日為休息例假，慶祝日、端午、中秋節各放假一日。

translations.literal: The days of the lunar mansions Fang, Xu, Xing, and Mao were regular rest days; celebrated days, the Dragon Boat Festival, and the Mid-Autumn Festival each had one day off.
translations.idiomatic: Regular rest days fell on Fang, Xu, Xing, and Mao; celebrated days, the Dragon Boat Festival, and the Mid-Autumn Festival each brought one day off.

sentences.zh: 每年以正月二十日開學，至小暑節散學，為第一學期。

translations.literal: Each year school opened on the twentieth day of the first month and closed at the Minor Heat solar term, constituting the first term.
translations.idiomatic: The first term opened on the twentieth day of the first month and closed at Minor Heat.

sentences.zh: 立秋後六日開學，至十二月十五日散學，為第二學期。

translations.literal: School opened six days after the Beginning of Autumn and closed on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month, constituting the second term.
translations.idiomatic: The second term opened six days after Beginning of Autumn and closed on the fifteenth of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 學生賞罰，由教員、監學摘出，監督核定。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments for students were proposed by teachers and student supervisors and confirmed by the superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers and student supervisors proposed rewards and punishments, which the superintendent confirmed.

sentences.zh: 賞分三種：曰語言獎勵，曰名譽獎勵，曰實物獎勵。

translations.literal: Rewards were of three kinds: verbal encouragement, honorific recognition, and material rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards took three forms: verbal praise, honors, and material prizes.

sentences.zh: 罰分三種：曰記過，曰禁假，曰出堂。

translations.literal: Punishments were of three kinds: demerit records, denial of leave, and expulsion from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments took three forms: demerit marks, denial of leave, and expulsion.

sentences.zh: 學生以端飭品行為第一要義，監督、監學及教員隨時稽察，詳定分數，與科學分數合算。

translations.literal: Proper conduct was the first requirement for students; the superintendent, student supervisors, and teachers inspected at all times, assigning detailed scores that were combined with academic scores.
translations.idiomatic: Proper conduct came first: the superintendent, student supervisors, and teachers watched students constantly, graded conduct in detail, and combined those scores with academic marks.

sentences.zh: 學堂考試分五種：曰臨時考試，曰學期考試，曰年終考試，曰畢業考試，曰升學考試。

translations.literal: School examinations were of five kinds: informal tests, term examinations, year-end examinations, graduation examinations, and advancement examinations.
translations.idiomatic: School examinations fell into five types: spot tests, term exams, year-end exams, graduation exams, and promotion exams.

sentences.zh: 臨時試無定期，學期、年終、畢業考試分數與平日分數平均計算。

translations.literal: Informal tests had no fixed schedule; scores from term, year-end, and graduation examinations were averaged together with daily scores.
