translations.idiomatic: Spot tests had no fixed schedule; term, year-end, and graduation marks were averaged with daily grades.

sentences.zh: 年考及格者升一級，不及格者留原級補習，下屆再試，仍不及格者退學。

translations.literal: Those who passed the annual examination advanced one grade; those who failed remained in the same grade for remedial study and were tested again the following year; if they still failed, they were dismissed from school.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the annual exam advanced a student one grade; failure meant repeating the year and retesting; a second failure brought dismissal.

sentences.zh: 評定分數，以百分為滿格，八十分以上為最優等，六十分以上為優等，四十分以上為中等，二十分以上為下等，謂之及格，二十分以下為最下等，應出學。

translations.literal: Scores were graded on a hundred-point scale: eighty or above was highest excellence, sixty or above excellence, forty or above middling rank, twenty or above lowest passing rank—all called passing; below twenty was the lowest rank and required leaving school.
translations.idiomatic: Grades ran to one hundred points: eighty or above counted as highest excellence, sixty as excellence, forty as middling, twenty as lowest pass—all deemed passing; below twenty was failing and meant leaving school.

sentences.zh: 畢業考試最重，視學堂程度，由所在地方官長會同監督、教員親蒞之，照鄉會試例。

translations.literal: Graduation examinations were the most important; according to the level of the school, local officials together with the superintendent and teachers presided in person, following the model of the provincial and metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Graduation exams mattered most: according to a school's level, local officials joined the superintendent and teachers in presiding, on the model of the provincial and metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 高等學畢業，簡放主考，會同督、撫、學政考試。

translations.literal: For graduation from higher schools, chief examiners were appointed and conducted examinations jointly with governors-general, governors, and education commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Higher-school graduations were examined by appointed chief examiners together with governors-general, governors, and education commissioners.

sentences.zh: 大學分科畢業，簡放總裁，會同學務大臣考試。

translations.literal: For graduation from university divisions, a chief superintendent was appointed and conducted examinations jointly with the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: University division graduations were examined by an appointed chief superintendent together with the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 分內、外二場：外場試，就學堂舉行。

translations.literal: Examinations were divided into inner and outer sessions: the outer session was held at the school.
translations.idiomatic: Exams were split into outer and inner sessions; the outer session was held at the school.

sentences.zh: 擇各科講義精要一二條摘問，令諸生答述。

translations.literal: One or two key points from each subject's lectures were selected for questioning, and students were asked to expound their answers.
translations.idiomatic: One or two essential points from each subject's lectures were chosen for questioning, and students answered orally.

sentences.zh: 內場試，擇地扃試。

translations.literal: The inner session was held at a selected sealed examination site.
translations.idiomatic: The inner session was held at a sealed examination site.

sentences.zh: 分兩場：首場以中學發題，經、史各一，經用論，史用策。

translations.literal: It was divided into two sessions: the first session used Chinese learning as topics—one on the classics and one on history; the classics by discourse essay, history by policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: The inner exam had two parts: the first tested Chinese learning with one classics essay and one history policy question.

sentences.zh: 二場以西學發題，政、藝各一，西政用考，西藝用說。

translations.literal: The second session used Western learning as topics—one on Western politics and one on Western arts; Western politics by examination questions, Western arts by explanatory essays.
translations.idiomatic: The second tested Western learning with one question on Western politics and one explanatory essay on Western arts.

sentences.zh: 通儒院畢業，不派員考試，以平日研究所得各種著述，評定等第，進呈，候欽定。

translations.literal: Graduates of the Academy of Universal Learning were not examined by appointed officials; their various writings produced through daily research were graded and submitted for imperial confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: Academy of Universal Learning graduates were not examined by appointed officials; their research writings were graded and submitted for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 其獎勵章程，比照獎勵出洋遊學日本學生例，通儒院畢業，予以翰林升階，或分用較優京、外官。

translations.literal: The reward regulations followed the precedent for students who studied abroad in Japan: graduates of the Academy of Universal Learning were granted Hanlin advancement or assigned to relatively superior capital or provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards followed the precedent for students sent to study in Japan: Academy graduates received Hanlin advancement or assignment to better capital or provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 大學分科畢業，最優等作為進士出身，用翰林院編修、檢討。

translations.literal: University division graduates of highest excellence were granted jinshi status and appointed as Hanlin compilers or reviewers.
translations.idiomatic: University division graduates of highest excellence received jinshi status and appointment as Hanlin compilers or reviewers.

sentences.zh: 優等、中等均作為進士出身，分別用翰林院庶吉士、各部主事。

translations.literal: Those of excellence and middling rank were likewise granted jinshi status and appointed respectively as Hanlin probationers or departmental secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Those of excellence and middling rank also received jinshi status and appointment as Hanlin probationers or departmental secretaries.

sentences.zh: 大學選科，比照分科大學降等給獎。

translations.literal: University elective students received awards scaled down from those for the full divisions.
translations.idiomatic: University elective students received reduced awards compared with full division graduates.

sentences.zh: 大學豫備科及各省高等學畢業，最優等作為舉人，以內閣中書、知州用。

translations.literal: Graduates of university preparatory programs and provincial higher schools of highest excellence were granted juren status and appointed as Grand Secretariat secretaries or prefects.
translations.idiomatic: University preparatory and provincial higher-school graduates of highest excellence received juren status and appointment as Grand Secretariat secretaries or prefects.

sentences.zh: 優等、中等均作為舉人，以中書科中書、部司務、知縣、通判用。

translations.literal: Those of excellence and middling rank were likewise granted juren status and appointed as Secretariat secretaries, departmental clerks, magistrates, or assistant prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Those of excellence and middling rank also received juren status and appointment as secretaries, departmental clerks, magistrates, or assistant prefects.

sentences.zh: 中學畢業，分別獎以拔貢、優貢、歲貢。

translations.literal: Middle school graduates were rewarded respectively with the titles of chosen tribute student, excellent tribute student, and regular tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-school graduates were rewarded with the titles of chosen, excellent, or regular tribute student.

sentences.zh: 高等小學畢業，分別獎以廩、增、附生。

translations.literal: Higher primary school graduates were rewarded respectively with stipendiary, supplemented, and attached licentiate status.
translations.idiomatic: Higher primary graduates received stipendiary, supplemented, or attached licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 初等小學屬義務教育，不給獎。

translations.literal: Elementary primary schools were compulsory education and received no awards.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary primary education was compulsory and carried no awards.

sentences.zh: 優級師範畢業，最優等、優等、中等均作為舉人，分別以國子監博士、助教、學正用。

translations.literal: Higher normal school graduates of highest excellence, excellence, and middling rank were all granted juren status and appointed respectively as Imperial College instructors, assistant instructors, or educational directors.
translations.idiomatic: Higher normal graduates of highest excellence, excellence, and middling rank all received juren status and appointment as Imperial College instructors, assistant instructors, or educational directors.

sentences.zh: 初級師範畢業，分別獎以拔貢、優貢、歲貢，以教授、教諭、訓導用。

translations.literal: Elementary normal school graduates were rewarded respectively with chosen, excellent, and regular tribute student status and appointed as professors, instructors, or local education officers.
translations.idiomatic: Elementary normal graduates received chosen, excellent, or regular tribute student status and appointment as professors, instructors, or local education officers.

sentences.zh: 高等實業學堂畢業，最優等、優等、中等均作為舉人，分別以知州、知縣、州同用。

translations.literal: Higher vocational school graduates of highest excellence, excellence, and middling rank were all granted juren status and appointed respectively as prefects, magistrates, or sub-prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Higher vocational graduates of highest excellence, excellence, and middling rank all received juren status and appointment as prefects, magistrates, or sub-prefects.

sentences.zh: 中等實業學堂畢業，獎勵視中學。

translations.literal: Middle vocational school graduates received awards equivalent to those for middle schools.
translations.idiomatic: Middle vocational graduates received the same awards as middle-school graduates.

sentences.zh: 奏定章程規定之概要如此。

translations.literal: Such was the outline of what the approved regulations prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the outline of the approved regulations.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，詔以各省學堂次第興辦，必須有總匯之區，以資董率而專責成。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, an edict stated that as schools were being established in succession across the provinces, there had to be a central coordinating office to provide leadership and hold sole responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year an edict declared that as schools rose across the provinces, a central office was needed to lead the effort and hold sole responsibility.

sentences.zh: 特設學部，命榮慶為尚書，熙瑛、嚴修為侍郎。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Education was specially established, with Rong Qing appointed Minister and Xi Ying and Yan Xiu appointed Vice Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Education was created, with Rong Qing as Minister and Xi Ying and Yan Xiu as Vice Ministers.

sentences.zh: 裁國子監，歸併學部。

translations.literal: The Imperial College was abolished and merged into the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial College was abolished and absorbed into the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 明年，學部奏請宣示教育宗旨，略言：「今中國振興學務，宜注重普通教育，令全國之民無人不學。

translations.literal: The following year, the Ministry memorialized requesting that the educational aim be proclaimed, stating in summary: "At present, in revitalizing China's educational affairs, emphasis should be placed on general education, so that no person throughout the country remains uneducated.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Ministry asked that the educational aim be proclaimed, writing in summary: "In reviving China's schools, the emphasis should fall on general education until every person in the country is taught.

sentences.zh: 尤以明定宗旨，宣示天下，為握要之圖。

translations.literal: Above all, to define the aim clearly and proclaim it to the realm is the essential measure."
translations.idiomatic: Above all, a clear aim proclaimed to the realm is the essential step."

sentences.zh: 中國政教所固有，亟宜發明以距異說者有二：曰忠君，曰尊孔。

translations.literal: Two principles inherent in China's government and teaching should urgently be expounded to repel heterodox doctrines: loyalty to the sovereign, and reverence for Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Two principles inherent in China's polity and teaching must urgently be upheld against heterodox doctrines: loyalty to the sovereign and reverence for Confucius.

sentences.zh: 中國民質所最缺，亟宜箴砭以圖振起者有三：曰尚公，曰尚武，曰尚實。

translations.literal: Three qualities most lacking in the Chinese people's character should urgently be corrected to bring revival: public spirit, martial spirit, and practical spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Three qualities most lacking in the national character must urgently be cultivated for renewal: public spirit, martial spirit, and practical spirit.

sentences.zh: 」上諭照所陳各節通飭遵行。

translations.literal: The throne ordered that each point raised be generally circulated and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered every point circulated and obeyed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 尋奏定學部官制，於本部各司、科分掌教育行政事務外，設編譯圖書局、調查學制局、京師督學局。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they memorialized to fix the organizational regulations of the Board of Education; apart from the various departments and sections of the ministry handling educational administration, they established the Bureau for Compiling and Translating Books, the Bureau for Investigating School Systems, and the Metropolitan Superintendency of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Education soon submitted regulations for its own organization; beyond the departments and sections that handled routine educational administration, it set up bureaus for compiling and translating books, investigating school systems, and supervising education in the capital.

sentences.zh: 又擬設高等教育會議所，屬學部長官監督。

translations.literal: They also proposed establishing a Higher Education Council, to be supervised by the senior officials of the Board of Education.
translations.idiomatic: It also proposed a Higher Education Council under the supervision of the Board's senior officials.

sentences.zh: 其議員選派部員，及直轄學堂、各省中等以上學堂監督，暨京、外官紳，學識宏通，於教育素有經驗者充任。

translations.literal: Its members were to be selected from among ministry staff, supervisors of schools under direct authority and of middle and higher schools in the provinces, as well as officials and gentry in the capital and elsewhere who were broadly learned and long experienced in education.
translations.idiomatic: Members were to include ministry staff, supervisors of directly administered and provincial middle and higher schools, and learned officials and gentry in the capital and provinces with long experience in education.

sentences.zh: 又擬設教育研究所，延聘精通教育之員，定期講演，以訓練本部員司焉。

translations.literal: They also proposed establishing an Educational Research Institute, engaging persons well versed in education to give lectures at fixed intervals in order to train the ministry's staff.
translations.idiomatic: It also proposed an Educational Research Institute that would engage education specialists to lecture on a regular schedule and train the ministry's own personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是直督袁世凱奏陳學務未盡事宜，以裁撤學政為言。

translations.literal: Previously the governor-general of Zhili, Yuan Shikai, had memorialized on unfinished matters in educational affairs, speaking in favor of abolishing the education commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhili governor-general Yuan Shikai had memorialized on remaining problems in educational administration, urging the abolition of education commissioners.

sentences.zh: 雲南學政吳魯奏請裁撤學政。

translations.literal: The education commissioner of Yunnan, Wu Lu, memorialized requesting the abolition of education commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan education commissioner Wu Lu likewise memorialized to abolish the post.

sentences.zh: 至是學部會同政務處復議，言：「各省教育行政及擴張興學之經費，督飭辦學之考成，與地方行政在在皆有關係。

translations.literal: At this time the Board of Education, together with the Bureau of Government Affairs, reconsidered the matter and stated: "Provincial educational administration, the funds for expanding school promotion, and the performance assessments for supervising schools are everywhere connected with local administration.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Education and the Bureau of Government Affairs then reconsidered the question and argued: "Provincial educational administration, the money needed to expand schooling, and the performance reviews for supervising schools are all bound up with local government at every turn.

sentences.zh: 學政位分較尊，事權不屬，於督、撫為敵體，諸事不便於稟承，於地方為客官，一切不靈於呼應。

translations.literal: Education commissioners hold a relatively exalted rank and their authority does not belong to the provincial chain of command; they stand as equals to governors-general and governors, making it inconvenient to report and receive orders on all matters; in the locality they are guest officials, and nothing responds readily to their calls.
translations.idiomatic: Education commissioners outranked local officials yet did not belong to the provincial chain of command; treated as equals of governors-general and governors, they could not easily report up or receive orders, and as outsiders in the province they found it hard to get anything done.

sentences.zh: 且地方寥闊，官立、公立、私立學堂日新月盛，勢不能如歲、科試分棚調考之例。

translations.literal: Moreover, the territory is vast; government, public, and private schools flourish day by day, and it is impracticable to follow the precedent of annual and supplementary examinations with separate examination sheds for invigilation.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces were vast, and government, public, and private schools were multiplying daily; it was impossible to keep up the old practice of touring separate examination sheds for annual and supplementary tests.

sentences.zh: 而循例按臨，更日不暇給。

translations.literal: Yet to make the rounds according to routine would leave not a day to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Even making the rounds on the old schedule would leave no day free.

sentences.zh: 勞費供張，無裨實事。

translations.literal: The labor, expense, and ceremonial arrangements would be of no help to practical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The labor, expense, and ceremonial display would do nothing for real educational work.

sentences.zh: 擬請裁撤學政，各省改設提學使司提學使一員，統轄全省學務，歸督、撫節制。

translations.literal: It is proposed to abolish education commissioners and in each province establish an Education Intendant's Office with one education intendant to superintend all provincial educational affairs, subject to the control of the governor-general and governor.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed abolishing education commissioners and replacing them in each province with a single education intendant, heading an Education Intendant's Office to oversee all provincial schools under the governor-general and governor.

sentences.zh: 於省會置學務公所，分曹隸事。

translations.literal: In the provincial capital a public education office is to be established, with sections subordinate to it for handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each provincial capital would have a public education office with specialized sections under it.

sentences.zh: 選派官紳有學行者，別設學務議紳四人，延訪本省學望較崇之紳士充選。

translations.literal: Officials and gentry of scholarly conduct are to be selected; four education advisers are to be separately appointed, chosen by inviting distinguished local scholars of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Learned officials and gentry would be chosen, and four education advisers appointed from the province's most respected scholars.

sentences.zh: 議長一人，學部慎選奏派。

translations.literal: One chair is to be appointed, carefully selected by the Board of Education and dispatched by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: One chair would be carefully chosen by the Board of Education and appointed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 嗣是各省學務始有確定之執行機關矣。

translations.literal: After this, the provinces at last had a fixed executive organ for educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, every province had a stable executive body for educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 勸學所之設，創始於直隸學務處。

translations.literal: The establishment of educational promotion offices originated with the Zhili Bureau of Educational Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Educational promotion offices were first created by the Zhili Bureau of Educational Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時嚴修任學務處督辦，提倡小學教育，設勸學所，為廳、州、縣行政機關。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Xiu served as superintendent of the bureau, promoting primary education; he established promotion offices as the administrative organs of prefectures, departments, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Xiu headed the bureau, he promoted primary education and set up promotion offices as the administrative organs of prefectures, departments, and counties.

sentences.zh: 仿警察分區辦法，采日本地方教育行政及學校管理法，訂定章程，頗著成效。

translations.literal: Following the police districting method and adopting Japanese local educational administration and school management law, regulations were drawn up with considerable success.
translations.idiomatic: Modeled on police districting and drawing on Japanese local educational administration and school-management law, the regulations proved notably effective.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，學部奏定勸學所章程，通行全國，即修呈訂原章也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the Board of Education memorialized to fix regulations for promotion offices and apply them nationwide—these were Yan's original regulations as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 the Board of Education memorialized regulations for promotion offices and applied them nationwide—the very rules Yan had drafted.

sentences.zh: 勸學所由地方官監督，設總董一員，以縣視學兼充，綜核各學區事務。

translations.literal: Promotion offices were supervised by local officials; one general director was appointed, concurrently serving as county school inspector, to oversee affairs in all school districts.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials supervised each promotion office; a general director, who also served as county school inspector, coordinated all school districts.

sentences.zh: 區設勸學員一人，任一學區內勸學之責，以勸募學生多寡，定勸學員成績之優劣。

translations.literal: Each district had one promotion officer bearing responsibility for encouragement of learning within the district; the number of students recruited determined the promotion officer's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Each district had one promotion officer responsible for recruiting students; performance was judged by how many pupils were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 其章程內推廣學務一條，規定辦法凡五：曰勸學，曰興學，曰籌款，曰開風氣，曰去阻力。

translations.literal: Within the regulations, the article on expanding educational affairs specified five methods: encouragement of learning, establishment of schools, fundraising, opening public sentiment, and removing obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: The section on expanding educational work listed five tasks: encouraging study, founding schools, raising funds, changing public attitudes, and removing obstacles.

sentences.zh: 又奏定各省教育會章程，省會設立者為總會，府、州、縣設立者為分會，以補助教育行政，與學務公所、勸學所相輔而行。

translations.literal: Regulations for provincial education associations were also memorialized: those established at provincial capitals were general associations, those at prefectures, departments, and counties were branch associations, to assist educational administration and work in concert with public education offices and promotion offices.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for provincial education associations followed: general associations at provincial capitals and branch associations in prefectures, departments, and counties, to assist educational administration alongside public education offices and promotion offices.

sentences.zh: 皆普及教育切要之圖也。

translations.literal: All were essential measures for spreading universal education.
translations.idiomatic: All were vital steps toward universal education.

sentences.zh: 學部設立後，於各項學堂章程多所更正。

translations.literal: After the Board of Education was established, many revisions were made to regulations for various schools.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Board of Education was in place, it revised regulations for many types of schools.

sentences.zh: 其要者，如改訂考試辦法，詳定師範獎勵義務，變通中、小學課程，中學分文科、實科之類，然大致不外修正科目，確定限制，其宏綱細目，不能出奏定章程之範圍。

translations.literal: The important ones included revising examination methods, specifying incentives and obligations for normal schools, adapting middle and primary school curricula, dividing middle schools into literary and practical tracks, and so forth; yet in general these amounted to no more than adjusting subjects and fixing limits—the broad outlines and detailed provisions could not go beyond the scope of the memorialized regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Major changes included new examination rules, clearer incentives and duties for normal schools, revised middle and primary curricula, and the division of middle schools into literary and practical tracks; but these were mostly adjustments to subjects and limits, and the broad framework still fell within the memorial-approved regulations.

sentences.zh: 所增定者，則女學堂章程也。

translations.literal: What was newly added was the regulations for girls' schools.
translations.idiomatic: The chief addition was a set of regulations for girls' schools.

sentences.zh: 先是學部官制已將女學列入職掌。

translations.literal: Previously the organizational regulations of the Board of Education had already listed girls' education among its duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Board's own organizational regulations had already placed girls' education within its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，奏定女子師範、女子小學章程，以裨補家計，有益家庭教育為要旨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, regulations for women's normal schools and women's primary schools were memorialized and fixed, with assisting the household economy and benefiting home education as the main purposes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1907 regulations for women's normal and primary schools were approved, emphasizing support for household economy and improvement of home education.

sentences.zh: 師範科目：修身、教育、國文、歷史、地理、算學、格致、圖畫、家事、裁縫、手藝、音樂、體操。

translations.literal: Normal school subjects: ethics, education, Chinese, history, geography, mathematics, natural science, drawing, domestic affairs, sewing, handicrafts, music, gymnastics.
translations.idiomatic: Normal-school subjects were ethics, pedagogy, Chinese, history, geography, mathematics, natural science, drawing, domestic science, sewing, handicrafts, music, and gymnastics.

sentences.zh: 四年畢業。

translations.literal: Four years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: The course ran four years.

sentences.zh: 音樂得隨意學習。

translations.literal: Music might be studied at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Music was optional.

sentences.zh: 小學分兩等，高等科目：修身、國文、算術、中國歷史、地理、格致、圖畫、女紅、體操，得酌加音樂，為隨意科。

translations.literal: Primary schools were divided into two levels. Higher level subjects: ethics, Chinese, arithmetic, Chinese history, geography, natural science, drawing, needlework, gymnastics; music might be added at discretion as an optional subject.
translations.idiomatic: Primary schools had two levels. The higher level taught ethics, Chinese, arithmetic, Chinese history, geography, natural science, drawing, needlework, and gymnastics, with music optional.

sentences.zh: 初等科目：修身、國文、算術、女紅、體操，得酌加音樂、圖畫二隨意科。

translations.literal: Elementary level subjects: ethics, Chinese, arithmetic, needlework, gymnastics; music and drawing might be added at discretion as two optional subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The elementary level taught ethics, Chinese, arithmetic, needlework, and gymnastics, with music and drawing optional.

sentences.zh: 均四年畢業。

translations.literal: Both four years to graduation.
translations.idiomatic: Both levels required four years.

sentences.zh: 其授業鐘點，較男子小學減少，與男子小學分別設立，不得混合。

translations.literal: Their instructional hours were fewer than those of boys' primary schools; they were to be established separately from boys' primary schools and not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Instructional hours were shorter than in boys' primary schools; girls' schools were to be separate and not combined with boys' schools.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年。

translations.literal: The third year of Xuantong.

sentences.zh: 奏設中央教育會議，以討論教育應行改進事宜及推行方法。

translations.literal: A Central Education Conference was memorialized and established to discuss matters requiring educational reform and methods of implementation.
translations.idiomatic: A Central Education Conference was established to discuss needed reforms and how to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 則根據學部原奏，擬設高等教育會議所之規定行之。

translations.literal: This was carried out according to the original Board of Education memorial proposing a Higher Education Council.
translations.idiomatic: It followed the Board of Education's earlier proposal for a Higher Education Council.

sentences.zh: 此為第二期有系統之教育制度也。

translations.literal: This was the systematic educational system of the second period.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the systematic educational order of the second period.

sentences.zh: 至考驗遊學畢業生，光緒二十九年，鄂督張之洞奏准鼓勵遊學章程。

translations.literal: As for examining students returning from study abroad: in the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu, the governor-general of Hubei, Zhang Zhidong, memorialized and received approval for regulations encouraging study abroad.
translations.idiomatic: As for examining students returning from study abroad, Hubei governor-general Zhang Zhidong had won approval in 1903 for regulations encouraging overseas study.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，學務大臣考驗北洋學生金邦平等，援照鄉、會試覆試例，奏請在保和殿考試，給予出身，分別錄用。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, the Minister of Education examined Beiyang students including Jin Bangping; following the precedent of re-examination at provincial and metropolitan examinations, he memorialized requesting examinations in the Hall of Preserving Harmony, granting degrees, and assigning appointments accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 the Minister of Education examined Beiyang students such as Jin Bangping and, following the precedent of provincial and metropolitan re-examinations, asked that they be tested in the Hall of Preserving Harmony, granted degrees, and appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 迨三十二年，學部奏定，自本年始，每年八月舉行一次。

translations.literal: By the thirty-second year, the Board of Education memorialized and fixed that from that year onward the examination would be held once each year in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 the Board of Education fixed annual examinations beginning that year, to be held each eighth month.

sentences.zh: 並為綜覈名實起見，妥議考驗章程。

translations.literal: To verify reputations against actual achievement, examination regulations were carefully drafted.
translations.idiomatic: To match credentials to real accomplishment, it also drafted careful examination rules.

sentences.zh: 將學成試驗與入官試驗分為兩事，酌照分科大學及高等學畢業章程，會同欽派大臣，按所習學科分門考試。

translations.literal: The graduation examination and the civil-service examination were divided into two matters; following the regulations for specialized universities and higher schools, jointly with imperially appointed officials, examinations were administered by field according to subjects studied.
translations.idiomatic: Graduation testing and entry into office were separated; following the regulations for specialized universities and higher schools, imperially appointed officials would examine candidates by field of study.

sentences.zh: 酌擬等第，候欽定分別獎給進士、舉人等出身。

translations.literal: Grades were provisionally proposed, awaiting imperial confirmation for granting jinshi, juren, and other degrees respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Grades were proposed pending imperial approval, with jinshi, juren, and other degrees awarded accordingly.

sentences.zh: 仍將某科字樣加於進士等名目之上，以為表識。

translations.literal: The name of the field was still added to titles such as jinshi as a mark of identification.
translations.idiomatic: The field of study was still prefixed to titles such as jinshi for identification.

sentences.zh: 考試分兩場：第一場就所習學科擇要命題；

translations.literal: The examination was divided into two sessions: the first session set questions by selection from the subjects studied;
translations.idiomatic: The examination had two parts: the first tested the candidate's major subjects;

sentences.zh: 第二場試中國文、外國文，罷廷試。

translations.literal: the second session tested Chinese and foreign languages, and the palace examination was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: the second tested Chinese and a foreign language, and the palace examination was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明年，學部憲政編查館會奏遊學畢業廷試錄用章程，仍暫照三十一年成案。

translations.literal: The following year the Board of Education and the Constitutional Compilation and Investigation Office jointly memorialized regulations for palace examination and appointment of students returning from study abroad, temporarily following the thirty-first-year precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Board of Education and the Constitutional Compilation and Investigation Office jointly submitted rules for palace examination and appointment of returned students, temporarily following the 1905 arrangement.

sentences.zh: 於欽派大臣會同學部考試請予出身後，廷試一次，分別授職。

translations.literal: After imperially appointed officials together with the Board of Education examined candidates and petitioned for granting degrees, one palace examination was held and appointments were assigned accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: After imperial appointees and the Board examined candidates and petitioned for degrees, a palace examination was held once more and offices were assigned.

sentences.zh: 廷試用經義、科學、論、說各一，其醫、工、格致、農等科大學及各項高等實業學堂畢業者，免試經義。

translations.literal: The palace examination used one essay each on classical meaning, science, disquisition, and exposition; graduates of medical, engineering, natural science, and agricultural universities and of higher vocational schools were exempt from the classical-meaning essay.
translations.idiomatic: The palace test required one essay each on classical interpretation, science, disquisition, and exposition; graduates of medical, engineering, natural science, and agricultural universities and of higher vocational schools were exempt from the classical essay.

sentences.zh: 時遊學日本、歐、美畢業回國者，絡繹不絕，歲舉行考驗以為常，終清世不廢。

translations.literal: At the time graduates returning from study in Japan, Europe, and America came in an unbroken stream; annual examinations became the norm and were not abandoned until the end of the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates returning from Japan, Europe, and America now arrived in a steady flow; annual examinations became routine and continued until the dynasty's end.
